Esketamine alleviates the pain-depression dyad: insights from exploratory transcriptomic profiling and Wnt4-associated molecular alterations within the anterior cingulate cortex.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: The molecular mechanisms driving esketamine (ESK) efficacy in the pain-depression dyad (PDD) remain incompletely understood. This study investigated the effects of a sub-anesthetic ESK regimen on cortical expression profiles and exploratory signaling markers within the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC). METHODS: Male Sprague-Dawley rats were randomized into Sham, PDD, and PDD + ESK groups. The PDD model, established via chronic constriction injury (CCI), was validated using a behavioral test battery tracking mechanical allodynia and depression-like phenotypes. On day 21 post-surgery, PDD + ESK rats received a single esketamine injection (15 mg/kg, i.p.). Multi-regional c-Fos expression mapping across the PFC, HPC, and ACC identified the primary responsive structure, followed by dual immunofluorescence for cellular phenotyping. Finally, ACC excitatory neuronal calcium dynamics, exploratory transcriptomic profiles, and Wnt4-associated molecular alterations (including GSK3β and mTOR phosphorylation alongside synaptic markers) were evaluated using fiber photometry, RNA sequencing, and Western blotting. RESULTS: ESK alleviated pain hypersensitivity, behavioral despair, and anhedonia in PDD rats. Regional c-Fos profiling identified the ACC as the primary reactive locus, with activation localized predominantly to CaMKIIα-positive neurons. Fiber photometry confirmed that ESK attenuated functional hyperactivation in these ACC excitatory neurons. Exploratory transcriptomic profiling (unadjusted P < 0.05) revealed candidate altered transcripts, identifying Wnt4 as an exploratory molecular marker for further investigation. Subsequent orthogonal protein validations demonstrated that ESK modulated Wnt4 expression alongside concomitant alterations in GSK3β and mTOR phosphorylation, parallel with the attenuation of pathologically elevated synaptic protein markers and a restorative trend in synaptic ultrastructure. CONCLUSION: A single sub-anesthetic ESK dose effectively alleviates PDD behavioral phenotypes in rats. This therapeutic efficacy is associated with Wnt4-related molecular adjustments coupled with putative downstream GSK3β-mTOR signaling alterations within the ACC CaMKIIα-positive neurons, providing exploratory transcriptomic and molecular insights into cortical adaptations in pain-related affective disorders.

articles.title: Comparison of azithromycin and doxycycline for the treatment of Chlamydia psittaci pneumonia.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Chlamydia psittaci pneumonia (CPP) has received increasing clinical attention worldwide in recent years. Although doxycycline is the recommended first-line therapy and macrolides serve as alternatives, no studies have directly compared their clinical efficacy in the general adult population. This study aimed to compare clinical outcomes between doxycycline and azithromycin in adult patients with CPP. METHODS: This retrospective single-center cohort study included 57 adult patients with CPP at Peking University Third Hospital from 2021 to 2025, of whom 31 received doxycycline and 26 received azithromycin. Demographic characteristics, laboratory findings, and clinical outcomes were compared between the two groups. RESULTS: Baseline characteristics, including comorbidities and laboratory findings, were comparable between groups. Respiratory support requirements and glucocorticoid use were similar (all P > 0.05). A numerical imbalance in Intensive Care Unit (ICU) admission rate was observed, with 16.1% in the doxycycline group and 0% in the azithromycin group (P = 0.056); this difference likely reflects treatment-selection bias given the small sample size. No significant differences were observed in 28-day discharge rate (96.8% vs. 100%), mortality (3.2% vs. 0%), median length of hospital stay (6 vs. 6 days, P = 0.691), or time to defervescence (2 vs. 2 days, P = 0.436). CONCLUSION: No statistically significant differences were observed in measured short-term clinical outcomes between doxycycline and azithromycin for CPP. Both may be reasonable therapeutic options, but findings should be interpreted cautiously given limited statistical power and potential confounding by indication, especially where drug availability or susceptibility data are limited.

articles.title: The Schisandra-Salvia-Hawthorn herbal formulation demonstrates therapeutic efficacy in ameliorating hyperlipidemia.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: This study investigates the potential efficacy and action mechanism of a herbal formulation comprising Schisandra chinensis, Salvia miltiorrhiza and Hawthorn (SSH) in the treatment of hyperlipidemia. METHODS: A hyperlipidemic cell model was established by free fatty acid (FFA)-induced HepG2 cells and a hyperlipidemic mouse model was established by high-fat diet (HFD)-induced C57BL/6 mice. Cell viability of HepG2 cells was assessed by MTT assay. Serum lipid profiles (TC, TG, LDL-C, HDL-C) were quantified via the corresponding kits. Hepatic tissue pathology was evaluated via Oil Red O staining and HE staining. Serum inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α and IL-6) were measured through ELISA. The mRNA and protein expression of seven key targets (APOB, LDLR, OLR1, PPARG, PRKCA, RXRA, NCF1) identified via network pharmacology prediction, were detected using qRT-PCR and Western blot. Besides, protein levels of p-p65 and p65 were detected by Western blot. Immunofluorescence staining was used to monitor p65 subcellular distribution, and DCFH-DA-based fluorescence detection was conducted to assess ROS production. RESULTS: In FFA-induced HepG2 cells, TC, TG, and lipid accumulation were reduced after SSH treatment. In HFD-induced mice, SSH treatment attenuated HFD-induced increases in serum TC, TG, and LDL-C levels, while elevating the level of HDL-C. It also reduced hepatic lipid accumulation, hepatic injury and expression of TNF-α and IL-6. Mechanistically, SSH formulation reversed HFD-driven dysregulation of the predicted targets: it downregulated the expression of APOB, OLR1, PRKCA, RXRA, PPARG and NCF1, and upregulated the expression of LDLR. FFA caused increases of OLR1 protein expression, PRKCA protein expression and phosphorylation of NF-κB p65 as well as ROS production in HepG2 cells, which were reversed by SSH treatment. CONCLUSION: The SSH formulation mitigated hyperlipidemia by restoring lipid homeostasis and suppressing inflammation. Its efficacy was mediated through a multi-target mechanism, coordinately regulating lipoprotein metabolism (APOB/LDLR), oxidative stress and inflammatory signaling (OLR1/PRKCA/NCF1), and nuclear receptor activity (PPARG/RXRA).

articles.title: Pregnancy and perinatal outcomes following exposure to GLP-1 and dual GLP-1/GIP receptor agonists: a time-window-stratified systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: To evaluate maternal, fetal, and neonatal outcomes after preconception or gestational exposure to glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and dual glucagon-like peptide-1/glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide receptor agonists, and to assess the reproducibility of reported safety signals. METHODS: Six databases plus a drug-level safety search were searched through 16 July 2026. Exposure was classified into four clinically defined time windows. Independent studies or data sources were the analytic unit; one primary comparator was selected per study, and odds ratios and risk ratios were synthesized separately. Random-effects meta-analysis, timing-stratified and dominant-study sensitivity analyses, Newcastle-Ottawa Scale assessment, and GRADE certainty assessment were used. RESULTS: Fourteen comparative data sources were included; 13 were quantitatively eligible and eight contributed to at least one pooled estimate. In the timing-specific analysis of major congenital malformations, four studies with verified periconceptional/first-trimester exposure yielded an odds ratio of 0.99 (95% confidence interval 0.77-1.27). A secondary pregnancy-period analysis that added one unadjusted, trimester-unspecified cohort yielded 1.00 (0.94-1.06); that cohort contributed 93.5% of the weight. Pooled preterm birth, small-for-gestational-age birth, and stillbirth analyses showed no statistically significant differences. Preeclampsia and other sparse outcomes were not pooled. Certainty was very low for all key outcomes. CONCLUSION: Current evidence does not demonstrate a clear or consistent increase in major congenital malformation risk, but very low certainty, imprecision, residual confounding, heterogeneous comparators, sparse agent-specific data, and uncertain exposure timing preclude conclusions of safety. Reported preeclampsia and renal or urinary signals have not been independently replicated.

articles.title: Benzoylaconine suppresses colorectal cancer progression by modulating the CDK2/MMP2 signaling axis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Colorectal cancer (CRC) has a high incidence, and both metastasis and drug resistance remain formidable challenges in clinical management. Owing to their multi-target activity and favorable safety profiles, natural products have become a prolific source for anticancer drug discovery. Benzoylaconine (BAC) is a secondary metabolite of aconitine with markedly attenuated toxicity that retains anti-inflammatory, analgesic, and antitumor properties; however, its antitumor effects and the underlying molecular mechanisms in CRC are poorly defined. This study was designed to systematically characterize the impact of BAC on the malignant phenotypes of CRC cells and to identify its potential molecular targets. METHODS: HCT116 and SW480 cells were used as model systems. Proliferation was assessed by MTT and EdU assays; migration and invasion by wound-healing and Transwell assays, respectively; cell cycle and apoptosis by flow cytometry. Network pharmacology was applied to predict core targets and construct a protein-protein interaction network. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations examined binding; SPR verified direct binding to CDK2 and MMP2. RNA-seq identified differentially expressed genes and enriched pathways. Western blotting validated key protein changes. Patient-derived CRC organoids (PDOs) were established to evaluate BAC efficacy; organoid viability was assessed by CellTiter-Glo® 2.0 assay, and morphology by bright-field microscopy. RESULTS: BAC dose- and time-dependently inhibited CRC cell proliferation and EdU positivity, slowed wound closure, and reduced Transwell invasion, indicating impaired migration and invasion. Flow cytometric analysis revealed that BAC induced G1/S cell cycle arrest and apoptosis. Network pharmacology identified CDK2 and MMP2 as key targets; molecular dynamics and SPR confirmed stable binding (KD ≈ 3.9 and 4.4 μM). RNA-seq showed enrichment of pathways related to cell cycle regulation and tumor invasion. Western blotting revealed that BAC dose-dependently downregulated CDK2, CDK6, MMP2, Cyclin E1, and Cyclin D1, and upregulated p21. BAC also inhibited the proliferation of colorectal cancer organoids. CONCLUSION: BAC induces G1/S cell cycle arrest in CRC cells, likely through modulation of the CDK2/MMP2 signaling axis, thereby suppressing proliferation, migration, and invasion while promoting apoptosis, and may represent a promising lead for CRC therapy.

articles.title: Trans-anethole attenuates streptozotocin-induced cognitive dysfunction by modulating oxidative stress and cholinergic activity.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Cognitive impairment is a neurological disorder defined as an inability to learn, think, judge, remember, and make decisions. The primary cause of chronic, age- related cognitive decline is Alzheimer's disease (AD), which is frequently studied as a representative model. The current therapies for AD provide only symptomatic relief, which necessitates the need for safer, multi-target treatments. Trans- anethole, the primary constituent of Illicium verum, Pimpinella anisum, and Foeniculum vulgare, is an aromatic molecule that possesses several pharmacological activities, including anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects, which may have neuroprotective benefits. METHODS: The current study integrated in silico, in vitro, and in vivo approaches to examine the neuroprotective potential of trans- anethole. In silico studies were carried out to find out the potential molecular targets and pathways associated with the effects of trans-anethole against AD- related cognitive dysfunction. Cytotoxicity, antioxidant activity, and cholinesterase inhibition were assessed in vitro on BV2 cells. Intracerebroventricular (ICV) administration of streptozotocin (STZ: 3 mg/kg) in rats induces an insulin-resistant brain state leading to progressive cognitive and memory impairment, a condition that closely relates to sporadic Alzheimer's disease. ICV-STZ-induced Wistar rats were used to assess the effect of trans- anethole on AD-related cognitive dysfunction through behavioral, biochemical, and histopathological assessments. RESULTS: A total of 174 common targets were identified, enriching pathways including apoptosis, AGE-RAGE, TNF, and PI3K- Akt signaling. Stable interactions were observed in molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations. Trans-anethole demonstrates moderate cholinesterase inhibition and antioxidant activity in BV2 cells. Comparing STZ- treated rats to disease control, trans-anethole at doses of 100 mg/kg and 400 mg/kg significantly reduced lipid peroxidation, restored antioxidant enzyme levels, and attenuated cholinergic dysfunction. Histopathological findings showed qualitative preservation of hippocampal neuronal morphology. DISCUSSION: Overall, these findings suggest that trans-anethole may represent a potential neuroprotective preclinical candidate for further investigation in Alzheimer's disease-related cognitive dysfunction.

articles.title: Clinical characteristics and pharmacovigilance signals of immune checkpoint inhibitor-associated cystitis and ureteritis: analysis of FAERS reports and published cases.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI)-associated cystitis and ureteritis are uncommon urinary immune-related adverse events that are difficult to distinguish from infection or other urinary tract complications. Their clinical phenotype and pharmacovigilance signal remain incompletely defined. METHODS: We combined a pooled analysis of published cases with a FAERS disproportionality analysis from 2004Q1 to 2026Q1. Published cases were reviewed for clinical presentation, treatment, rechallenge, and time-to-onset. FAERS reports were deduplicated at the CASEID level. A broad cystitis-inclusive definition included IMMUNE-MEDIATED CYSTITIS, CYSTITIS NONINFECTIVE, URETERITIS, and CYSTITIS; a high-specificity definition excluded the nonspecific Preferred Term CYSTITIS. Disproportionality was assessed using reporting odds ratios (RORs), proportional reporting ratios, chi-square statistics, and information components. RESULTS: Twenty-eight reports comprising 45 unique patients were included. The median age was 56 years, and lung cancer was the most common malignancy. Published cases commonly showed urinary frequency, dysuria, hematuria, leukocyturia, inflammatory imaging or cystoscopic abnormalities, and corticosteroid responsiveness. Upper urinary tract involvement was documented in 13 of 33 patients with available CT data. Median time-to-onset was 62 days among 24 evaluable cases, and recurrence occurred in 5 of 9 rechallenged patients. In FAERS, 20,257,224 deduplicated CASEIDs were analyzed. The broad cystitis-inclusive definition identified 397 ICI-associated cases and showed only a weak signal (ROR, 1.12; 95% CI, 1.02-1.24), whereas the high-specificity definition identified 151 cases and yielded a stronger signal (ROR, 9.04; 95% CI, 7.63-10.70). Class-level signals were also observed, and the overall high-specificity signal remained positive across sensitivity analyses. CONCLUSION: These findings support ICI-associated cystitis and ureteritis as an uncommon urothelial inflammatory irAE spectrum. Phenotype-aware outcome definition is important in pharmacovigilance because nonspecific cystitis coding may dilute the reporting signal.

articles.title: Hepatoprotective and pancreatoprotective effects of Arctium lappa root extract in valproic acid-induced toxicity: biochemical, histopathological, and immunohistochemical analysis.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Valproic acid (VPA) is a widely used antiepileptic drug; however, its clinical use is limited by hepatotoxicity and pancreatitis, primarily mediated through oxidative stress and inflammation. Arctium lappa root extract (ALRE) has been reported to possess antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and cytoprotective properties that may confer protection against VPA-induced organ toxicity. METHODS: Phytochemical profiling of ALRE was performed using GC-MS and HPLC. In vitro cytotoxic effects were assessed in Hep3B and PANC-1 cancer cell lines, while safety was assessed in THLE-2 normal hepatic epithelial cells and H6C7 normal pancreatic ductal epithelial cells using the MTT assay. The hepatoprotective and pancreatoprotective effects were investigated in VPA-induced toxicity in male Wistar albino rats through biochemical, oxidative stress, and histopathological analyses. RESULTS: ALRE exhibited low cytotoxicity towards THLE-2 and H6C7 cells, with IC50 values of 1,084.92 and 1,174.62 μg/mL, respectively. VPA administration markedly increased serum levels of ALT (127.67 ± 4.34 U/L), AST (153.67 ± 4.91 U/L), ALP (178.67 ± 5.21 U/L), GGT (7.67 ± 0.09 U/L), amylase (47.33 ± 2.91 U/L), and lipase (49.00 ± 3.79 U/L) compared with the control group (p < 0.05). These enzyme levels were considerably lowered by ALRE administration, especially at 500 mg/kg. Furthermore, ALRE restored antioxidant defences (SOD, CAT, and GSH), malondialdehyde levels were decreased, and the histological architecture of the liver and pancreas was improved. CONCLUSION: ALRE effectively attenuated VPA-induced hepatic and pancreatic injury through antioxidant and cytoprotective mechanisms while exhibiting minimal toxicity towards normal hepatic and pancreatic cells. These findings support the potential therapeutic application of A. lappa as a natural protective against VPA-associated hepatotoxicity and pancreatitis. Further studies are warranted to elucidate the molecular mechanisms and pharmacokinetic interactions underlying the protective effects of ALRE.

articles.title: Rutin interferes with hnRNP L phase separation and modulates the PKM2-lactate-H3K9la axis in pulmonary fibrosis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Pulmonary fibrosis is a chronic and progressive lung disease with limited treatment options; it is urgent to develop new drugs. PURPOSE: This study investigated the anti-pulmonary fibrosis effects and mechanism of rutin, and sought to provide a potential lead compound for further development of anti-pulmonary fibrosis agents. METHODS: The anti-pulmonary fibrosis effect of rutin was assessed using Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8), real-time cell proliferation analysis and scratch wound healing assay in Transforming Growth Factor-β1(TGF-β1)-stimulated Medical Research Council cell strain-5 (MRC-5) cells, along with lung function tests, MicroCT imaging, Hematoxylin and Eosin (H&E) and Masson staining in mice with induced pulmonary fibrosis. The mechanism of rutin was explored through molecular docking, the surface plasmon resonance assay, the cell thermal shift assay (CETSA), droplet formation observation, fluorescence recovery after photobleaching, transcriptome sequencing, Enzyme Linked Immunosorbent Assay (ELISA), Co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) and Chromatin Immunoprecipitation-Polymerase Chain Reaction (ChIP-PCR). RESULTS: Rutin inhibited fibroblast-to-myofibroblast differentiation, myofibroblast proliferation and migration, and extracellular matrix deposition. Moreover, rutin effectively improved lung function, including forced vital capacity, dynamic lung compliance and total lung capacity. Additionally, rutin markedly alleviated fibrotic features, such as honeycomb lung reduction, preserved alveolar structure and thinned alveolar walls. Mechanistically, our data support a model in which rutin may interfere with hnRNP L phase separation, and this interference is associated with reduced PKM2 generation, decreased lactate production and subsequent loss of H3K9la. The reduced H3K9la, in turn, correlated with suppressed PKM2 transcription, suggesting a self-limiting regulatory circuit. CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest that rutin may interfere with the regulatory interplay involving hnRNP L phase separation, PKM2 alternative splicing, lactate, and H3K9la, which is associated with the attenuation of pulmonary fibrosis. While these data reveal a potential mechanistic framework, definitive causality at each step of this regulatory axis remains to be established. Further studies are warranted to validate this model and to optimize the bioavailability of rutin for therapeutic application.

articles.title: Community Pharmacists' Perspectives and Experiences of Deprescribing in Québec, Canada: Findings From a Survey.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Community pharmacists in Quebec can bill for deprescribing. However, uptake remains low. We aimed to explore how community pharmacists perceive and engage in deprescribing. METHODS: Community pharmacists were invited to complete an online survey through a pharmacists' social media group and a newsletter. Data were analysed using descriptive statistics and univariate chi-square tests. RESULTS: Among 366 respondents, most were women (n = 269; 74%), worked full-time (n = 282; 77%), had time for clinical interventions (n = 223; 61%), while 53% (n = 193) had fewer than 11 years of experience. Three quarters (n = 271) reported initiating deprescribing at least monthly. Side effects (n = 273; 75%) and patients' requests (n = 220; 60%) were more common reasons for deprescribing. More than 70% (n = 268) reported that prescribers usually accepted recommendations. Initial and follow-up consultations were systematically billed by 50% (n = 183) and 48% (n = 174) of respondents, respectively. Deprescribing interventions and billing practices were more common among pharmacists with dedicated clinical time and those working full time (all p < 0.01). Main barriers to billing were insufficient training (n = 217; 59%), uncertainty about reimbursement eligibility (n = 127; 35%) and lack of time (n = 112; 31%). Integrated software was the most common facilitator (n = 246; 67%). CONCLUSION: Deprescribing was commonly reported among respondents and was often prompted by clinical concerns and patient requests. Billing uncertainties and time constraints remained important barriers, highlighting opportunities to better support deprescribing in community pharmacy.

articles.title: Dosing HIV integrase inhibitors with enzyme inducers: Convenience vs. control?
Tenofovir diphosphate intracellular concentration following tenofovir alafenamide administration in bictegravir-containing vs. dolutegravir-containing antiretroviral regimens.
articles.abstract: This study investigates intracellular (IC) exposure of tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) and its clinical determinants in experienced people living with HIV. We conducted a monocentric retrospective analysis of 86 adults treated with either bictegravir (BIC)- or dolutegravir (DTG)-containing regimen. Plasma and IC trough concentrations (Ctrough) of tenofovir diphosphate (TFV-DP) were examined in relation to demographic and renal parameters. A significant correlation emerged between plasma and IC TFV-DP Ctrough. Higher plasma TFV levels were associated with older age and reduced estimated glomerular filtration rate. Adherence calculated as proportion of days covered (PDC) did not differ between regimens. These findings provide novel real-world insights into IC TFV-DP pharmacokinetics and suggest that BIC-containing regimens may enhance IC drug accumulation, although the impact of this observation on virological outcomes requires further studies.

articles.title: Comparative treatment effects of direct oral anticoagulants versus warfarin for nonvalvular atrial fibrillation in clinical practice vary over time due to channelling.
articles.abstract: AIM: Temporal shifts in patient characteristics can influence comparative treatment effects within a certain indication. We investigated patient characteristics and comparative effectiveness and safety for direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) and warfarin over the time period where DOACs replaced warfarin as preferred stroke prophylaxis in patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation (NVAF). METHODS: We applied the cohort design to the Clinical Practice Research Datalink Aurum and created 12 sequential subcohorts of patients with NVAF between 2011 and 2023. Patients with a DOAC or warfarin prescription following a 1-year prescription-free period were included. Baseline characteristics were compared between subcohorts. Survival analysis was used to evaluate the risk of ischaemic stroke (effectiveness outcome) and major bleeds (safety outcome). RESULTS: We included 207 393 patients with NVAF (45% women, 77% DOAC users, mean age 76 years). In early subcohorts, a history of stroke/transient ischaemic attack was more common among DOAC users. In later subcohorts, diabetes, deep venous thrombosis/pulmonary embolism and antihypertensive use were more common among warfarin users. History of other cardiovascular disease, renal failure and diuretic use were consistently higher among warfarin users. Over time, the crude stroke hazard ratio for DOAC users compared with warfarin users shifted from 2.66 (95% CI 2.00-3.52) to 0.62 (0.23-1.67). This trend was attenuated in adjusted analyses. No such trends were seen for major bleeds. CONCLUSION: DOACs had unfavourable effectiveness estimates in earlier subcohorts, potentially due to preferential prescribing to higher risk patients. Early observational studies may encounter initial biases, underscoring the need for robust methodological approaches when evaluating newly introduced medicines.

articles.title: Study on the protective mechanism of Astragaloside IV by regulating the NETs pathway against ischemic stroke.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Ischemic stroke (IS) triggers systemic inflammatory immune response, increasing blood neutrophil count. Inflammatory factors from ischemic area recruit neutrophils to form neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs), worsening injury. Astragaloside IV (AS-IV) exhibits proven neuroprotective effects against cerebral ischemia, potentially through suppressing NETs. This study examines how AS-IV prevents cerebral ischemic injury by blocking NETs formation (NETosis). METHODS: The Phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA)-induced mouse bone marrow-derived neutrophils (BMNs) injury model was built to evaluate AS-IV's impact on NETosis, reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, and marker proteins via scanning electron microscopy, flow cytometry, immunofluorescence techniques. AS-IV's protective action against NETs-damaged HT22 cells was elucidated via untargeted metabolomics. Targeted metabolomics for differential metabolites was carried out on a ultra-high performance liquid chromatography coupled with triple quadrupole mass spectrometry. AS-IV's impact on neurological features, regional cerebral blood flow (CBF), and inflammatory infiltrates in transient middle cerebral artery occlusion (tMCAO) was evaluated by behavioral assessment, laser speckle contrast imaging, histological sectioning. Combined with peptidyl arginine deiminase 4 (PAD4) inhibitor Cl-amidine, NETs-associated proteins in cerebral tissue were detected by western blot (WB) and immunohistochemistry (IHC), and serum MPO-DNA and NE-DNA levels were tested using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) to further elucidate AS-IV's mechanism against ischemic brain injury. RESULT: AS-IV dose-dependently inhibited NETs formation in PMA-induced mouse BMNs by reducing ROS levels and alleviating NETs-damaged HT22 cells. AS-IV reversed metabolic disorders in NETs-induced HT22 cells. Of the 14 differential metabolites detected, purine metabolism represented the predominantly altered metabolic pathway. Our in vivo data demonstrate that AS-IV improves neurological function, rescues impaired regional cerebral perfusion, and mitigates inflammatory cell infiltration. Mechanistically, these neuroprotective outcomes are largely attributed to the inhibition of PAD4-mediated NETosis.. CONCLUSION: AS-IV protects against ischemic brain injury by inhibiting PAD4-mediated NETosis.

articles.title: A novel coumarin-derived Schiff base ligand suppresses TLR-NFκB signalling and oxidative stress in vitro, and exhibits anticonvulsant activity in vivo.
articles.abstract: Neuroinflammation is a primary hallmark of chronic neurodegenerative diseases and is also implicated in poor outcomes following acute trauma and brain injury. Neuroinflammation arises largely from dysregulated activation of microglia, which disrupts neuronal function and promotes degradation of the blood-brain barrier. This, in turn, accelerates progressive neurotoxicity that characterises these conditions. Most neurodegenerative diseases are marked by a paucity of disease-modifying therapies, reflecting the complex, multicellular and multifaceted nature of their pathology. This presents a major challenge to the development of universally effective treatments. Activation of Toll-like receptors (TLRs), particularly TLR2 and TLR4, is widely reported to be a key driver of neuroinflammatory processes in these disorders. Naturally occurring agents, including coumarins, have been shown to downregulate TLR signalling and exert antioxidant effects under a number of disease-relevant conditions. We have previously reported the synthesis of a novel family of coumarin-derived Schiff base ligands with robust copper-complexing properties. In this study, we explored the bioactivity of one such ligand, L4, in the context of neuroinflammatory diseases. In particular, we examined the impact of L4 on microglial activation and neurotoxicity in vitro and on survival and behaviour in zebrafish models of inflammation and neuronal stress in vivo. Our results revealed that L4 alleviated microglial inflammatory responses, likely through inhibition of the TLR-NFκB pathway. In addition, L4 conferred protection against oxidative stress-induced neurotoxicity and produced an anticonvulsant effect in a zebrafish seizure model. Taken together, our findings support further investigation of L4 as a potential multitarget therapeutic for neuroinflammatory and neurodegenerative diseases.

articles.title: Simple heat-assisted method for mRNA loading into empty lipid nanoparticles enables robust in vitro and in vivo delivery.
articles.abstract: mRNA-lipid nanoparticles (LNP) have emerged as a versatile modality, enabling diverse applications by changing encoded mRNA sequences. However, the conventional mRNA-LNP preparation process poses significant barriers to non-specialists because it requires specialized equipment and technical expertise. In this study, we aimed to report a simple post-encapsulation approach where mRNA is mixed with preformed empty LNP in solution to form mRNA-LNP for effective in vitro and in vivo delivery. Process optimization revealed that heating mRNA and empty LNP at 75°C and pH 4.0 achieved approximately 90% mRNA encapsulation while maintaining an LNP size of approximately 100 nm. The resulting post-encapsulated LNP were comprehensively compared with conventional LNP prepared via microfluidic mixing. Both LNP formulations exhibited over 90% cellular uptake and comparable concentration-dependent expression in vitro. The intravenous administration of post-encapsulated LNP in mice resulted in robust luciferase expression in the liver and spleen at 0.01 mg/kg, with no notable changes in serum chemistry at 1 and 3 mg/kg. However, the activity of the post-encapsulated LNP was slightly reduced compared with that of the conventional LNP. Sucrose density gradient centrifugation indicated that post-encapsulated mRNA-LNP formed heterogeneous populations with varying mRNA/lipid ratios, in contrast to conventional mRNA-LNP. These findings support a working hypothesis that this heterogeneity could contribute to the reduced in vivo activity. Our simple post-encapsulation method potentially could lower entry barriers for non-specialists in this field and accelerate RNA-LNP research through its compatibility with 96-well-format preparation.

articles.title: pH-regulated supersaturation enables nanonization of three model drugs for enhanced oral and transdermal delivery.
articles.abstract: Weakly ionizable drugs constitute the majority of clinically used small-molecule therapeutics; however, their pH-dependent solubility and permeability frequently result in poor bioavailability and suboptimal therapeutic efficacy. Herein, we developed a pH-regulated nanonization strategy that exploits the pKa-dependent solubility characteristics of weak electrolytes to generate drug nanoparticles through controlled supersaturation and polymer-assisted stabilization. Three representative weakly ionizable drugs with distinct ionization properties were selected as model compounds, including albendazole (ABZ, weak base), azelaic acid (AZA, weak acid), and hemin (amphoteric compound). The apparent solubilities of resulting nanoparticles (ABZNPs, AZANPs, and HNPs) increased by approximately 317-fold, 106-fold, and 1,100-fold, respectively, as compared to the corresponding free drugs. ABZNPs displayed excellent stability under simulated gastrointestinal conditions and significantly enhanced oral absorption in rats, yielding a 3.5-fold increase in Cmax and a relative bioavailability of 331.4% compared with a commercial formulation. Meanwhile, AZANPs markedly improved transdermal delivery, achieving 3.3-fold higher skin permeation and over twofold greater skin retention than the raw drug formulation. In a Cutibacterium acnes-induced acne model, a 5% AZANPs ointment achieved therapeutic efficacy comparable to that of a commercial 10% azelaic acid product while reducing local irritation. Mechanistically, AZANPs promoted PPAR-γ activation, suppressed inflammatory cytokine production, normalized epidermal hyperproliferation, and facilitated collagen remodeling. Collectively, In this study, we developed a pH-Regulated nanonization method and validated its feasibility using three model drugs, while acknowledging that its broader applicability warrants further investigation.

articles.title: Oral nicotine pouch extracts disrupt osteogenic differentiation in human embryonic stem cells.
articles.abstract: Oral nicotine pouch (ONP) use has increased in recent years due to the perception that these products are a safer alternative to combustible tobacco products. However, little is known about the potential developmental toxicity of ONPs, particularly during bone formation. In this study, we evaluated the effects of ONP extracts from multiple ZYN flavors and nicotine concentrations on osteogenic differentiation using a human embryonic stem cell (hESC) model. H9 hESCs were differentiated toward the osteogenic lineage and continuously exposed to ONP extracts throughout differentiation. Cellular metabolic activity was assessed using the MTT assay, while ATP content, total protein content, alkaline phosphatase (ALP) activity, glutathione peroxidase (GPx) activity, and calcium deposition were evaluated using biochemical assays and Alizarin Red S staining. Gene expression was assessed using RT-qPCR and single-cell RNA sequencing, followed by pseudotime trajectory and transcriptomic point of departure (tPOD) analyses. ONP exposure caused concentration-dependent reductions in MTT activity, ATP content, total protein content, ALP activity, GPx activity, and calcium deposition. Expression of the osteogenic marker RUNX2 was generally decreased following ONP exposure, while TWIST1, SOX10, and TBX5 expression were increased in several treatment groups. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis demonstrated significant alterations in cell cluster distribution and pseudotime trajectory following ONP exposure, suggesting disrupted osteogenic lineage progression. Transcriptomic analysis further identified widespread perturbation of bone development-related genes across treatments. Wintergreen 6 mg had among the greatest transcriptomic potency metrics. Together, these findings reveal that ONP extracts disrupt osteogenic differentiation in hESCs and alter developmental lineage progression. This study provides mechanistic evidence that oral nicotine pouch extracts perturb early osteogenic differentiation in a human stem cell model and supports further evaluation of their developmental toxicity.

articles.title: Evaluating the effects of xylazine on fentanyl-induced respiratory depression and recovery with rescue agents in rats.
articles.abstract: Despite the decrease in fatal opioid overdoses in the United States, fentanyl remains a major contributor to drug overdose deaths accounting for about 92% of opioid overdose deaths. Fentanyl is a mu opioid receptor agonist that is increasingly found in illicit drug mixtures containing alpha-2 adrenergic receptor agonists like xylazine. This study examined the effects of fentanyl and xylazine alone and in combination at an approximately 1:3 fentanyl-to-xylazine mass ratio, selected based on the reported composition of the Philadelphia drug supply. Whole-body plethysmography was used to assess respiratory function and the effects of rescue agents. Fentanyl alone (0.01 - 0.056 mg/kg, iv) produced dose-dependent decreases in tidal volume and minute volume, whereas xylazine alone (0.1 and 0.178 mg/kg, iv) did not produce significant changes in these respiratory parameters. Although respiratory depression did not differ significantly between fentanyl alone and the fentanyl-xylazine combination, the addition of xylazine altered the temporal pattern and persistence of fentanyl-induced changes in respiratory frequency, tidal volume, and minute volume. Co-administration of naloxone and atipamezole produced a rapid and sustained increase in respiratory activity, combining the rapid response observed with naloxone and the sustained response observed with atipamezole. These findings suggest that xylazine may alter the time course of fentanyl-induced respiratory depression and thereby complicate overdose reversal.

articles.title: In Vitro Anti-Inflammatory and Cytokine-Inhibitory Properties of Satureja nabateorum Extract: UPLC-ESI-QTOF-MS/MS Profiling and iNOS-Targeted Molecular Modeling.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Satureja nabateorum (Nabatean savory) is an Arabian medicinal plant traditionally used for inflammatory conditions, but its anti-inflammatory potential and metabolic profile remain insufficiently investigated. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study evaluated the anti-inflammatory potential of S. nabateorum and characterized its metabolites using integrated in vitro, metabolomic, and computational approaches. MATERIALS AND METHODS: The ethyl acetate (EA) fraction was evaluated in lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated RAW 264.7 macrophages for nitric oxide (NO) production, Map2k7 (MKK7) expression, and pro-inflammatory cytokines. Metabolites were tentatively annotated by UPLC-ESI-QTOF-MS/MS, followed by ADMET screening, target prediction, and molecular docking/dynamics against inducible nitric oxide synthase (iNOS; PDB ID: 3E6T). RESULTS: The EA fraction suppressed NO production dose-dependently (IC50 = 80.8 μg/mL), reduced IL-1β, IL-6, IFN-γ, and TNF-α expression, and partially reversed the LPS-induced decrease in Map2k7 expression. Profiling tentatively identified 51 metabolites, predominantly flavonoids, terpenoids, phenylpropanoids, sterols, and fatty acids. Kaempferitrin was prioritized computationally and showed favorable predicted interaction with iNOS (docking score -8.6753 kcal/mol). Redocking reproduced the experimental binding pose (RMSD = 1.4724 Å), while 100-ns molecular dynamics supported persistence of the modeled association. CONCLUSION: S. nabateorum exhibits significant in vitro anti-inflammatory. Kaempferitrin was tentatively identified and computationally highlighted as a potential contributor; its role in the observed activity requires validation through isolation, direct iNOS assays, and subsequent in vivo and clinical investigation.

articles.title: A polysaccharide from Tetrastigma hemsleyanum Diels & Gilg alleviates experimental colitis by restoring AMPK-TFAM-associated mitochondrial DNA quality control.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Tetrastigma hemsleyanum Diels & Gilg (Sanyeqing) is used in Chinese folk medicine for febrile and inflammatory disorders. Its polysaccharide fraction has shown intestinal protective activity, but the mitochondrial mechanism remains unclear. AIM OF THE STUDY: To determine whether a chemically and structurally characterized T. hemsleyanum polysaccharide (THP) alleviates experimental colitis in association with improved mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) homeostasis and mitochondrial quality-control responses. MATERIALS AND METHODS: THP was purified and characterized by chromatographic, spectroscopic, and compositional analyses. Its effects were examined in dextran sulfate sodium-induced acute colitis in mice and lipopolysaccharide/tert-butyl hydroperoxide-injured Caco-2 cells. Mucosal injury, barrier function, mitochondrial redox status and respiration, cytosolic mtDNA, TFAM distribution, autophagy-lysosome-related markers, and AMPK-PGC1α-NRF1-TFAM and cGAS-STING signaling were evaluated. Dorsomorphin and bafilomycin A1 were used to assess the contribution of AMPK signaling and lysosome-dependent autophagic flux. RESULTS: THP reduced disease activity, histological injury, inflammatory cytokines, and barrier disruption. It lowered cellular and mitochondrial ROS, improved mitochondrial morphology, membrane potential, respiration, and ATP production, and reduced cytosolic mtDNA accumulation. THP increased AMPK-PGC1α-NRF1-TFAM-related signaling and increased the spatial association of TFAM-positive mitochondrial material with LC3- and LAMP1-positive structures. Dorsomorphin or bafilomycin A1 attenuated several THP-associated effects. THP also reduced cGAS-STING, NF-κB, and NLRP3 pathway activation. CONCLUSIONS: THP ameliorated experimental colitis in association with improved mitochondrial redox and bioenergetic function, preservation of mtDNA homeostasis, and AMPK-TFAM-related mitochondrial quality control. The data support autophagy-lysosome involvement in the handling of TFAM-positive mtDNA-containing mitochondrial material, but do not establish selective nucleoid degradation. These findings support further investigation of THP as a mitochondria-targeted intestinal protective polysaccharide.

articles.title: EWM-CRITIC-VIKOR framework reveals mechanistic insights of Buyang Huanwu Decoction in ischemic stroke with experimental validation.
articles.abstract: ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Buyang Huanwu Decoction (BYHWD), a classical formula recorded in Yilin Gaicuo, has been widely used for the treatment of stroke and post-stroke sequelae in traditional Chinese medicine. AIM OF THE STUDY: This study aims to establish a novel framework based on the EWMCRITIC-VIKOR algorithm to prioritize potential BYHWD targets against IS by integrating multi-dimensional biological features, with validation through in vivo experiments. MATERIALS AND METHODS: 14 biological features across 4 dimensions were quantified. Feature weights were calculated using EWM and CRITIC, and integrated via VIKOR for MCDM on BYHWD-IS overlapping targets. The therapeutic effects of BYHWD were validated in middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) rat model. Anti-inflammatory effects were assessed by RT-qPCR and ELISA, while western blotting were used to evaluate signaling via the PI3K/AKT/NF-κB pathway. RESULTS: The EWM-CRITIC-VIKOR framework prioritized 5 key targets (FOS, IL1β, AKT1, TP53, and IL6) from 239 overlapping targets. The VIKOR compromise solution exhibited a distinct low-Q priority set, in which the top targets jointly minimized group utility and individual regret, and the overall ranking showed weak association with logFC, indicating that prioritization was not driven by expression effect size alone. BYHWD treatment significantly improved MCAO-induced brain injury. RT-qPCR and ELISA showed marked downregulation of IL1B and IL6 after BYHWD treatment, and western blotting indicated altered PI3K/AKT/NF-κB signaling status. CONCLUSION: The EWM-CRITIC-VIKOR framework enables robust prioritization of therapeutic targets by integrating heterogeneous biological data. This approach enhances mechanistic understanding of BYHWD in IS and offers a reliable strategy for target discovery in herbal interventions.

articles.title: Repeated swim exposure and PKN1a knockout enhance group I mGluR-dependent excitability associated with reduced EAAT3 expression in mouse dentate granule cells.
articles.abstract: Stress-related experiences alter glutamatergic signaling and neuronal excitability, but the mechanisms that couple experience to dentate granule cell function remain incompletely understood. Here, we examined how protein kinase N1a (PKN1a), a protein kinase C-like serine/threonine kinase, and repeated swim exposure regulate mouse hippocampal dentate granule cell excitability, with a focus on the neuronal glutamate transporter excitatory amino acid transporter 3 (EAAT3) and group I metabotropic glutamate receptors (mGluRs). Five days of repeated swim exposure increased spike firing in mature dentate granule cells from wild-type mice. PKN1a knockout produced a similar increase, and repeated swim did not further enhance firing in knockout mice. The enhanced firing observed after repeated swim exposure and in PKN1a knockout mice was reduced by co-application of an mGluR1 antagonist (LY367385) and an mGluR5 antagonist (MPEP). Inhibition of glutamate transporters with DL-TBOA increased granule cell firing in control wild-type mice but did not further increase firing in repeated-swim wild-type or PKN1a knockout mice, suggesting occlusion of transporter-dependent regulation of excitability. Repeated swim exposure and PKN1a knockout also reduced total and surface expression of EAAT3 in the hippocampus, whereas expression of the glial glutamate transporter EAAT2 was not significantly altered. Finally, PKN1a knockout and repeated swim exposure reduced anxiety-related behavior in the elevated plus maze test. Thus, PKN1a-dependent regulation of EAAT3 may restrain group I mGluR-dependent excitability in dentate granule cells, whereas repeated swim exposure and PKN1a knockout shift this system toward a lower-EAAT3, higher-excitability state accompanied by reduced anxiety-related behavior.

articles.title: Brain CYP2D alters orally administered oxycodone induced conditioned place preference in rats.
articles.abstract: Oxycodone is an opioid analgesic metabolized by the CYP2D enzyme to oxymorphone. We investigated in rats the impact of CYP2D metabolism in the brain on oxycodone-induced reward and aversion, assessed by conditioned place preference (CPP). During conditioning rats were confined to one compartment for 60 minutes after gavage with oxycodone (or oxymorphone) or with water; treatment and compartments were alternated daily for six days. Rats then underwent 60 minutes of posttests for five days where CPP was assessed. Pretreatments with the CYP2D inhibitor propranolol, or vehicle, injected intracerebroventricularly 24 hours - prior to first and third of six conditioning sessions blunted CPP and with a trend for increased aversion to the oxycodone paired compartment. Pretreatment with the brain CYP2D enzyme inducer nicotine, for 12 days prior to oxycodone conditioning, did not change CPP to oxycodone but tended to reduced aversion to oxycodone paired compartment. Oral oxymorphone induced a CPP with no observed aversion; it was unaffected by CYP2D inhibitor pretreatment. Together this indicates that oral oxycodone and oral oxymorphone both induce CPP. Inhibiting brain CYP2D, previously shown to reduce the relative concentrations of oxycodone to oxymorphone, reduces CPP and tended to increase aversion suggesting that variation in CYP2D activity in the brain could be a source of interindividual differences in oxycodone induced reward and abuse liability.

articles.title: Surface-modified liposomes with polyvinyl alcohol derivatives improve mucus penetration and oral absorption: A potential alternative to polyethylene glycol.
articles.abstract: Polyethylene glycol-modified (PEG-modified) nanocarriers are widely used as mucus-penetrating systems for oral administration. In this study, we developed a low-molecular-weight polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) bearing alkyl groups at molecular ends as a potential alternative to PEG for imparting mucus permeability to nanocarriers. We also evaluated its effects on mucus permeability and its applicability to oral drug delivery. The particle sizes of PVA-modified liposomes (PVA-Lip) and PEG-modified liposomes (PEG-Lip) were approximately 150 nm and 130 nm, respectively, and both exhibited monodisperse size distributions. PVA-Lip showed greater apparent mucus permeability than PEG-Lip. Furthermore, when liposomes encapsulating fluorescein isothiocyanate-dextran with an average molecular weight of 3,000-5,000 (FD4) as a peptide model were orally administered to rats, PVA-Lip and PEG-Lip exhibited similar overall FD4 absorption, with insignificant differences in the area under the plasma concentration-time curve (AUC). In repeated oral administration studies, the AUC of PEG-Lip decreased by approximately 43 % compared with the initial dose, whereas that of PVA-Lip decreased minimally. This decreased AUC may be associated with antibody responses, and PVA-Lip may be less susceptible to antibody-related effects than PEG-Lip. Collectively, these findings suggest that alkyl-terminated PVA could be an alternative to PEG for oral delivery.

articles.title: Biotin and TAT dual-stage targeting polymersomes for improved nuclear delivery of doxorubicin.
articles.abstract: A dual-stage targeting Pluronic F127/polylactic acid (PLA) polymersome modified with biotin (cell surface targeting) and trans-activator of transcription (TAT, cell nucleus targeting) [Biotin(TAT)-F127-PLA] was prepared by the biotin-avidin bridging technology to inhibit multidrug resistance (MDR) of cancer cells. Hydrophilic doxorubicin (DOX) was loaded into the polymersome to obtain Biotin(TAT)-F127-PLA/DOX with a size of 127.4 ± 1.7 nm. Its loading efficiency and loading capacity were 23.3% and 8.8%. The cytotoxicity of Biotin(TAT)-F127-PLA/DOX with different molar ratios of Biotin to TAT against doxorubicin-resistant A549/ADR and A549 human non-small-cell lung cancer cells followed the order: 10%:10% > 10%:5% > 10%:20% > 10%:30%. Biotin(TAT)-F127-PLA/DOX showed stronger cytotoxicity, better cellular and nuclear uptake than single-ligand and nontargeted polymersomes. Notably, even though the cellular uptake of TAT-F127-PLA/DOX was 0.95 times that of Biotin-F127-PLA/DOX, it achieved 1.02-fold nuclear uptake compared with Biotin-F127-PLA/DOX, demonstrating the nuclear-localization ability of TAT ligands. The uptake of Biotin(TAT)-F127-PLA/DOX by A549/ADR cells was proved to be related to the endocytosis mediated by biotin receptor. In addition, MDR mechanism study showed that the ability of Biotin(TAT)-F127-PLA/DOX to reduce adenosine-triphosphate (ATP) content and increase reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels in A549/ADR cells was better than other DOX-loaded polymersomes. More importantly, the tumor volume relative to the start point of 4T1 tumor-bearing mice intraperitoneally injected with Biotin(TAT)-F127-PLA/DOX polymersomes was only 451.06% at day 15 at an ultralow DOX dose (0.2 mg/kg), which was 25.09% of that treated with free DOX, indicating the superior tumor growth inhibition of the dual-stage targeting polymersome.

articles.title: STUB1/CYLD targets VDAC1 to regulate osteogenic differentiation in osteoporosis via modulating its ubiquitination and oligomerization.
articles.abstract: Osteoporosis (OP) constitutes a major global public health burden whose progression is closely linked to mitochondrial dysfunction and disrupted mitophagy homeostasis. This study was designed to characterize the critical function of voltage-dependent anion-selective channel protein 1 (VDAC1), an outer mitochondrial membrane channel protein, in OP and clarify the underlying mechanisms of VDAC1 modulating osteoblastic differentiation of BMSCs via its own ubiquitination and oligomerization under the action of STUB1/CYLD. Bioinformatic analysis of postmenopausal osteoporosis dataset GSE230665 identified VDAC1 as a core node linking mitophagy and osteoporosis. In vivo, AAV9-VDAC1 overexpression vector (AAV9-OE-VDAC1) alleviated osteoporotic phenotypes in ovariectomized (OVX) mice. In vitro, VDAC1 overexpression restored mitophagy and facilitated osteogenic differentiation of hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) -damaged bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs). VDAC1's stability is finely tuned by post-translational ubiquitination: STIP1 homology and U-box containing protein 1 (STUB1), an E3 ubiquitin ligase, triggers VDAC1 degradation through K48- and K63-linked ubiquitination, whereas cylindromatosis tumor suppressor (CYLD), a deubiquitinase, stabilizes VDAC1 by removing K63 ubiquitin chains. Oxidative stress induces aberrant VDAC1 oligomerization to suppress mitophagy and osteogenesis, which is rescued by oligomer inhibitor VBIT-4. Upregulated ubiquitination of VDAC1 aggravates its pathological oligomerization, forming a mutually reinforcing vicious cycle. Pharmacological inhibition of these two modifications could delay osteoporosis progression under experimental conditions. Collectively, targeting the STUB1/CYLD-VDAC1 axis to restore mitophagy and rescue impaired osteogenic differentiation of BMSCs may provide a potential research perspective for developing therapeutic strategies against OP.

articles.title: CLDN18.2-targeted CAR-NK cells suppress gastric cancer growth in preclinical models.
articles.abstract: Targeted immunotherapy for gastric cancer (GC) remains challenging due to safety concerns and limited efficacy against solid tumors. Claudin-18.2 (CLDN18.2) is a highly specific tumor-associated antigen, yet existing CLDN18.2-targeted CAR-T therapies are frequently complicated by cytokine release syndrome (CRS) and on-target/off-tumor toxicity. Natural killer (NK) cells represent a safer "off-the-shelf" alternative, but require optimized CAR architectures for effective solid tumor targeting. Here, we designed five CAR constructs targeting CLDN18.2 through combinatorial optimization of single-chain variable fragments and intracellular co-stimulatory domains (including CD28H, 2B4, 4-1BB, and CD3ζ), and delivered them into NK-92 cells via a baboon envelope glycoprotein-pseudotyped lentiviral vector. The lead candidate CAR4-NK, which harbors a CD28H-2B4-CD3ζ signaling domain, exerted superior in vitro cytotoxicity against CLDN18.2-positive GC cells, accompanied by robust secretion of IFN-γ and granzyme B. In NCG mouse xenograft models, intravenously administered CAR4-NK cells specifically trafficked to tumor sites, significantly suppressed tumor growth, and improved overall survival (100% survival at the study endpoint). The CD28H-2B4 combination was shown to be critical for sustained NK cell activation. Notably, irradiated CAR4-NK cells, despite abrogated proliferative capacity, retained tumoricidal efficacy comparable to unmodified parental NK-92 cells and induced minimal production of the inflammatory cytokines TNF-α and MIP-1α, suggesting a reduced risk of CRS-associated cytokine release within the tested panel. These results provide preclinical proof-of-concept for a rationally designed CAR4-NK therapy against CLDN18.2-positive gastric cancer, in which CD28H-2B4 co-stimulatory domains enhance the effector function of CAR4-NK cells, and show the potential of irradiated CAR4-NK cells as a safer, controllable "off-the-shelf" product candidate.

articles.title: Lead alleviates cadmium hepatotoxicity by remodeling its coordination environment: A combined XAFS and DFT study.
articles.abstract: Cadmium (Cd) and lead (Pb) frequently co-occur in contaminated environments, yet the toxicological interaction between them remains unclear. Here, we established a rat model of combined Cd and Pb exposure and used FTIR, synchrotron XAFS, and DFT calculations to examine the coordination mechanism underlying Pb-mediated modulation of Cd hepatotoxicity. Pb co-exposure significantly attenuated Cd-induced liver injury, as shown by reduced serum ALT, ALP, and GGT levels and alleviated histopathological damage. Spectroscopic and computational analyses revealed that Pb alters the local coordination environment of Cd by competing for oxygen-containing ligands in GSH and bridging sulfur atoms in MT, thereby weakening Cd-S interactions and promoting Cd redistribution from LCF-derived free Cd2+ fraction to GSH-/MT-bound forms. Pb co-exposure alleviates Cd-induced hepatotoxicity, and this effect is associated with changes in Cd coordination chemistry, underscoring the importance of metal speciation in assessing mixed-metal exposure risk.

articles.title: QTMP, a microtubule-depolymerizing agent, induces autophagy in neuroblastoma cells.
articles.abstract: Microtubule-targeting agents are highly effective chemotherapeutic agents against cancer, yet their role in modulating complex cellular pathways, such as autophagy, remains poorly understood. In this study, we report that a novel microtubule-depolymerizing antiproliferative agent, 5-(quinolin-2-yl)-4-(3,4,5-trimethoxyphenyl)-1H-imidazol-2-amine (QTMP), induces autophagy in neuroblastoma cells (SH-SY5Y and IMR-32). QTMP demonstrated potent cytotoxicity against SH-SY5Y and IMR-32 neuroblastoma cells, with half-maximal inhibitory values of 21 ± 1 nM and 9.3 ± 1.3 nM, respectively. A brief exposure to QTMP depolymerized microtubules, whereas prolonged exposure resulted in mitotic arrest in SH-SY5Y cells. Furthermore, QTMP caused mitochondrial dysfunction and increased reactive oxygen species production. Microtubule disruption induced oxidative stress and triggered autophagy in QTMP-treated cells, as evidenced by increased microtubule-associated protein 1A/1B light chain 3-II (LC3-II) formation, upregulation of ATG-5, and degradation of p62. Autophagy flux was further confirmed by increased monomeric red fluorescent protein-LC3 puncta in QTMP-treated cells. Importantly, QTMP exhibited a synergistic effect with the autophagy inducer rapamycin and an antagonistic effect with the autophagy inhibitors 3-methyladenine and SAR405, indicating that autophagy contributes to QTMP's cytotoxic mechanism in SH-SY5Y neuroblastoma cells. Similar to QTMP, colchicine and vinblastine also induced autophagy in SH-SY5Y cells, suggesting that autophagy induction is a consequence of microtubule disruption. The findings highlight QTMP as a promising therapeutic candidate that exerts cytotoxic effects by depolymerizing microtubules, inducing mitochondrial dysfunction, increasing reactive oxygen species production, and activating cytotoxic autophagy in neuroblastoma cells. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: This study identifies QTMP (5-(quinolin-2-yl)-4-(3,4,5-trimethoxyphenyl)-1H-imidazol-2-amine), a potent analog of combretastatin A-4, as a promising therapeutic candidate for neuroblastoma. QTMP induces cell death by depolymerizing microtubules, thereby causing severe mitochondrial dysfunction, increased oxidative stress, and subsequent activation of cytotoxic autophagy. These findings provide new insight into the cellular mechanisms of QTMP and highlight the involvement of cytotoxic autophagy in its anticancer activity against neuroblastoma cells.

articles.title: A previously undetected major circulating metabolite of trazpiroben revealed by human radiolabeled absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion study.
articles.abstract: Trazpiroben (TAK-906) is a dopamine D2/D3 receptor antagonist developed for the treatment of gastroparesis. In a human absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion (ADME) study, metabolite M50 was identified as the most abundant circulating metabolite following a single oral administration of 50 mg [14C]trazpiroben to healthy male participants, representing 32.4% of total plasma radioactivity. Despite its prominent contribution to circulating radioactivity, M50 accounted for only 0.34% of the administered dose recovered in the excreta. M50 was identified as isophthalic acid. It had not been identified in prior in vitro metabolism studies, preclinical radiolabeled ADME studies, or a human metabolite scouting study. Follow-up microsomal investigations did not detect M50 directly; however, trace levels of a related counterpart metabolite were observed in rat, dog, and human liver microsomes, indicating that the upstream oxidative dealkylation pathway was operative. Subsequent reaction phenotyping demonstrated that conversion of the proposed aldehyde intermediate to M50 was mediated by cytosolic aldehyde dehydrogenases. The failure to detect M50 in earlier studies was attributed to a combination of poor ionization efficiency, minor fractional formation, incomplete representation of the sequential metabolic pathway in microsomal incubations, and apparent species differences in metabolite formation and disposition. These findings demonstrate how highly polar and poorly ionizing metabolites may evade liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry-based profiling approaches despite representing major circulating drug-related material in humans and highlight the complementary value of radiolabeled human ADME studies for comprehensive metabolite characterization. They also highlight the importance of selecting appropriate in vitro systems for metabolism studies. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: A highly polar and poorly ionizing metabolite, isophthalic acid (M50), was identified as the major circulating metabolite of trazpiroben in a human radiolabeled absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion study despite not being detected in prior in vitro, preclinical, or clinical metabolite profiling studies. Mechanistic studies demonstrated that M50 formation required sequential metabolism involving aldehyde dehydrogenases. These findings highlight how metabolites formed through minor metabolic pathways may evade liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry-based profiling approaches yet represent major circulating drug-related material in humans.

articles.title: Review of the selectivity of chlorzoxazone 6-hydroxylation as a probe for human cytochrome P450 2E1.
articles.abstract: A recent article has criticized the use of chlorzoxazone 6-hydroxylation as a marker of human cytochrome P450 2E1 activity (Hellmann A et al. Challenging the specificity of chlorzoxazone and 4-nitrophenol as marker substrates for CYP2E1 activity in Supersomes. Arch. Toxicol. 2026:10.1007/s00204-026-04515-8), concluding that the activity is more reflective of hepatic cytochrome P450 1A1. We review previous literature that was overlooked, in support of this marker as being excellent for cytochrome P450 2E1. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: Chlorzoxazone 6-hydroxylation is a well established marker of human cytochrome P450 2E1 activity, which is needed for the evaluation of drug interactions. We discuss some recent objections, which were already addressed in earlier literature.

articles.title: Natural circular peptides regulate T-lymphocyte proliferation by inhibiting prolyl oligopeptidase.
articles.abstract: Peptide natural products are a promising source of bioactive molecules. Antiproliferative activity on stimulated T-lymphocytes has been associated with plant-derived cyclic cystine-rich peptides from the Rubiaceae family. In this study, we report a correlation between the peptide diversity in eleven Psychotria extract samples, their prolyl oligopeptidase (POP) inhibitory activity, and antiproliferative effects on stimulated T-lymphocytes. The peptide fraction enriched with cyclotides from Psychotria solitudinum was primarily responsible for the antiproliferative activity, with low cytotoxicity compared to other extracts. We used the prototypic peptide psysol 2 to show that inhibition of POP was key, while inhibitors targeting prolyl oligopeptidases dipeptidylpeptidase-4 (DPP4) and fibroblast activation protein alpha (FAPα) did not yield the same phenotype. Interestingly, POP protein expression and enzymatic activity significantly increased in stimulated T-lymphocytes at 72 h post-activation, suggesting a role for POP in T-cell activation and proliferation. Unlike the prototype immunomodulatory cyclotide T20K, the POP inhibitors psysol 2 and KYP-2047 did not significantly affect NF-κB-dependent gene expression and pro-inflammatory cytokine expression on the mRNA level. However, POP inhibitors reduced caspase 3 and caspase 8 activation induced by T-cell receptor (TCR) and CD3 restimulation, providing partially protection of T-lymphocytes from AICD. Psysol 2 appears to be a new immunomodulatory cyclic cystine-rich peptide that functions via altered T-cell receptor-dependent caspase signaling in a POP-associated mechanism. Overall, this study provides new insights into the T-cell antiproliferative activity of natural cyclic peptides and their anti-inflammatory properties.

articles.title: Urinary tract and genital infections with dapagliflozin and empagliflozin across type 2 diabetes, heart failure, and chronic kidney disease: An indication- and sex-stratified disproportionality analysis of eudravigilance reports.
articles.abstract: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors are widely used in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), chronic heart failure (CHF), and chronic kidney disease (CKD). Although their cardiovascular and renal benefits are well established, urogenital infections remain a relevant safety concern. Comparative post-marketing data on dapagliflozin (DAPA) and empagliflozin (EMPA) across therapeutic indications are limited. A retrospective pharmacovigilance analysis of the EudraVigilance database (January 2021-July 2025) was conducted using a case/non-case approach. Cases were defined as individual case safety reports (ICSRs) containing at least one urogenital infection-coded reaction and a confirmed indication (T2DM, CHF, or CKD). The primary analysis was restricted to reports originating from the European Economic Area (EEA), where reporting rules are identical for both drugs; reports with unspecified patient age were excluded. Among 16,102 EEA ICSRs, 8156 adult reports with a confirmed indication were analyzed, of which 1109 met the case definition. Non-EEA reports were analyzed separately as a sensitivity analysis. Urogenital infection reporting did not differ between DAPA and EMPA, overall (ROR 0.91; 95% CI 0.80-1.03) or within any indication (T2DM: 13.9% vs 14.9%, ROR 0.92; 95% CI 0.79-1.07; CHF: 11.5% vs 12.6%, ROR 0.90; 95% CI 0.69-1.18; CKD: 11.0% vs 6.7%, ROR 1.73; 95% CI 0.75-3.99). For both drugs, reporting was higher in T2DM than in CHF (DAPA ROR 1.25; 95% CI 1.00-1.56; EMPA ROR 1.22; 95% CI 0.99-1.51), a difference confined to female patients (DAPA 1.38; EMPA 1.56) and, in the endpoint disaggregation, to genital mycotic infections (DAPA 2.24; EMPA 1.79) rather than non-mycotic urogenital infections. Female sex was the strongest determinant of urogenital infection reporting for both drugs (ROR female/male 1.85 for DAPA and 1.58 for EMPA). In non-EEA reports, an apparent excess of urogenital infection reporting with DAPA over EMPA (ROR 1.85; 95% CI 1.59-2.16) was explained by a different composition of the reports forwarded for the two drugs rather than by a drug effect. Urogenital infection reporting with SGLT2 inhibitors depends on indication and sex rather than on the molecule, and between-drug comparisons in EudraVigilance are sensitive to the geographic origin of reports.

articles.title: Photothermally amplified NO release from arginine-encapsulated injectable nanocomposite hydrogel for triple-synergistic antitumor therapy.
articles.abstract: Monotherapeutics remain constrained by adaptive resistance mechanisms and inherent limitations imposed by tumor evolutionary pressure. Here, an injectable natural material-based hydrogel HC&Arg&Au/D was constructed to achieve multi-strategy combined anti-tumor therapy. Tyrosine-grafted hyaluronic acid (HA) achieved horseradish peroxidase (HRP)-catalyzed covalent crosslinking. 3-aminophenylboronic acid-modified carboxymethyl cellulose (CMC) formed pH-sensitive boronic ester bonds with HA's cis-diol groups, enabling acid-triggered degradation and drug release. Then, HC&Arg&Au/D hydrogel stably formed after subcutaneous implantation and safely degraded within three weeks, enabling sustained drug release at the tumor site. Specifically, doxorubicin (Dox) and gold nanoparticle (AuNP)-mediated photothermal therapy (PTT) synergistically induced tumor cell apoptosis and triggered immunogenic cell death (ICD). L-arginine (Arg) modulated the pH of the tumor microenvironment (TME), promoting the recruitment and polarization of M1 macrophages. Furthermore, the Arg/Au-containing hydrogel produced an NO assay signal under PTT and was associated with downregulation of the membrane transporter SLC7A11 and lipid peroxide accumulation. Because GPX4 protein abundance was unchanged, these findings support an additional redox contribution but do not by themselves establish canonical ferroptosis. These tightly coordinated therapeutic strategies collectively achieved remarkable anti-tumor efficacy, resulting in complete ablation of 4T1 orthotopic tumors in 40% of treated mice and significant volume reduction in remaining mice. This spatiotemporally controllable multimodal therapy system provides a basis for further study of functionalized hydrogel carriers that combine PTT, chemotherapy and immune modulation.

articles.title: Exploratory transcriptomic and network pharmacology prioritization of candidate targets and phytochemicals in vascular cognitive impairment.
articles.abstract: Vascular cognitive impairment (VCI) is closely associated with cerebral small vessel disease and is linked to increased disability, institutionalization and mortality, highlighting the need to identify biologically relevant therapeutic candidates. This study applied an exploratory transcriptomic and network pharmacology framework to prioritize candidate targets and phytochemicals relevant to VCI-associated molecular dysfunction. Analysis of the GSE201482 whole-blood dataset identified 1163 nominally differentially expressed genes between VCI and SCD/SVD comparator samples. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis identified trend-associated turquoise and green modules, yielding 352 overlapping DEG--WGCNA candidate genes. Integration with medicinal plant-derived compound targets identified 52 common candidate genes. Functional enrichment linked these genes to membrane-potential regulation, synaptic compartments, G-protein-coupled receptor signalling, oxidative stress response, hypoxia response, neuroactive ligand signalling and amino-acid metabolism. Immune deconvolution provided exploratory immune-context information on macrophage, monocyte, NK cell and T cell populations. Machine-learning feature prioritization using LASSO, Random Forest and SVM-RFE identified ACP1, CDC25A and MAO-B as candidate genes selected by all three algorithms. External assessment using the independent GSE303449 human brain RNA-seq dataset added a validation layer for candidate interpretation, although FDR-level support for the 52-gene signature and ML-derived panels was limited. MAO-B was selected for docking because it is a druggable neuroactive enzyme with established inhibitor biology and an experimentally resolved ligand-bound structure, enabling reference-based comparison with rasagiline. Docking analysis highlighted isorhamnetin, quercetin and oroxylin A as top-ranked phytochemicals against MAO-B. Overall, this study provides a reproducible candidate-prioritization workflow for guiding future experimental evaluation of multi-target phytochemical approaches in VCI.

articles.title: Safety, Pharmacokinetics, and Pharmacodynamics of SHR-2004, a Novel Humanized Monoclonal Antibody Targeting Factor XI, in Patients with Atrial Fibrillation: An Open-Label Phase 1b Study.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: SHR-2004, a humanized monoclonal antibody targeting factor XI (FXI), demonstrates potential for preventing and treating thrombotic events with reduced bleeding risk. This study evaluated the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics (PK), and pharmacodynamics (PD) of SHR-2004 in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). METHODS: In this open-label dose-escalation phase 1b study, patients with AF aged ≥ 40 and < 80 years with a CHA2DS2-VASc score ≥ 1 (male) or ≥ 2 (female) were enrolled to receive six doses of SHR-2004. The primary endpoints were safety and tolerability. PK and PD parameters, including activated partial thromboplastin time (aPTT) and FXI activity, were also assessed. RESULTS: From 10 April 2024 to 6 May 2024, ten patients were enrolled to receive SHR-2004 (180 mg subcutaneously, every 2 weeks), with a median age of 68.0 years, and male being in the majority (9/10). The median CHA2DS2-VASc score was 2.5 (range 1-6). The trial was terminated after completion of the 180 mg cohort. SHR-2004 was well tolerated. Treatment-emergent adverse events (AEs) occurred in eight (80.0%) patients, and treatment-related AEs were reported in six (60.0%) patients. All AEs were mild or moderate. Notably, no major or clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding events were reported. Plasma exposure of SHR-2004 increased rapidly after administration and reached steady state by day 57 with the geometric mean (CV%) plasma concentration of 24,000 (26.4) ng/mL. This exposure resulted in median FXI activity after the first dose of 1.40% (IQR 1.40-1.40%). The outcomes of PD effects, FXI activity and aPTT prolongation, reached a plateau during the treatment period from day 3 to day 85 indicating that the 180 mg dosage regimen achieved and maintained therapeutic pharmacodynamic steady state. CONCLUSIONS: Multiple subcutaneous doses of SHR-2004 were generally well tolerated in patients with AF. These preliminary findings support further clinical development of SHR-2004 in this population. TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: Clinicaltrials.gov identifier: NCT06280768. Trial registration date: 28 February 2024.

articles.title: Pharmacokinetic and abuse liability assessment of tobacco-flavored and menthol-flavored pod-based electronic nicotine delivery systems with 5% and 3% nicotine concentrations relative to combustible cigarettes.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Nicotine pharmacokinetics (PK) and subjective effects influence the abuse liability of electronic nicotine delivery systems (ENDS). This two-arm randomized crossover pharmacokinetic study assessed nicotine delivery from and subjective responses to four JUUL2 ENDS products (Virginia Tobacco and Fresh Menthol flavors [5% and 3% nicotine concentrations]) compared to combustible cigarettes and NJOY Ace (Classic Tobacco and Menthol flavors; 5% nicotine) among adult dual users. METHODS: Adults who smoked cigarettes daily and concurrently used ENDS (dual users) were assigned to one of two study arms based on whether they smoked nonmentholated cigarettes (Tobacco Arm [N = 30]) or mentholated cigarettes (Menthol Arm [N = 30]). On four consecutive study days participants first used each assigned product in a controlled use session (10 standardized 3-second puffs), and then, after ≥ 4 h of nicotine abstinence, in a 5-minute ad libitum use session. RESULTS: In both study arms and use conditions, peak nicotine delivery and total nicotine exposure from study ENDS products either did not statistically significantly differ from or was significantly lower than that of combustible cigarettes; time to maximum nicotine concentration did not significantly differ. All study ENDS products were rated as substantially less reinforcing than cigarettes, but similarly effective at reducing urge-to-smoke. CONCLUSIONS: The abuse liability profiles of all menthol-flavored and tobacco-flavored ENDS evaluated in this study were lower than cigarettes. The 5% nicotine ENDS products generally delivered comparable peak levels of nicotine and alleviated cravings for cigarettes to a similar extent as participants' usual brand cigarettes, suggesting they can be effective substitutes for cigarettes. CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: ISRCTN29801527 on October 25, 2024.

articles.title: Microdose jet injection reveals a tissue-dependent retention-expression window for carrier-free nucleic acid delivery.
articles.abstract: Efficient local nucleic acid delivery requires not only access to target cells but also retention of the administered payload. Yet whether increasing physical delivery input improves or compromises functional delivery remains poorly understood. Here, we show that microdose jet injection operates within a tissue-dependent retention-expression window that can be interpreted in terms of physical jet input. Using the Actranza Lab needle-free system, sub-microlitre to low-microlitre jet outputs were calibrated and characterised by high-speed imaging, defining a kinetic-energy range of approximately 0.38-18.5 mJ. Delivery outcomes were evaluated in mouse spleen, liver, and skin using dye-retention analysis and luciferase expression. In spleen and liver, low-volume jets were associated with local retention and high volume-normalised luciferase expression, whereas increasing jet input progressively increased retention failure and reduced expression efficiency despite larger administered DNA amounts. In contrast, skin maintained local retention over a substantially broader input range, and total luciferase expression showed a significant positive association with injection volume. At the same 1-µL splenic administration volume, Actranza Lab produced approximately 34-fold greater luciferase activity than a 30-G Hamilton microsyringe. Cross-tissue integration of retention-failure frequency and volume-normalised expression revealed narrower operational windows in spleen and liver and a broader window in skin. These findings show that successful carrier-free jet delivery is determined not by nominal dose alone, but by the interaction between physical jet input and tissue retention. This retention-expression framework provides a practical basis for tissue-specific optimisation of needle-free nucleic acid delivery.
