articles.title: Green synthesis of copper oxide nanoparticles ST@CuONPs by Streptomyces thinghirensis: current treatment path against multidrug-resistant bacteria.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Antibiotic resistance is currently a global concern, leading to serious complications in both clinical and non-clinical settings, and is particularly dreaded in developing countries. In the search for alternative treatments against bacterial infections, nanotechnology has opened up unexpected new horizons in the scientific world, thanks to the great variety of available nanomaterials that have potential antimicrobial activity. Some of the interest in this type of nanomaterials relies in their exceptional properties and usages in many fields. The investigation focused on the synthesis of a new copper oxide nanoparticles ST@CuONPs as a promising alternative to conventional antibiotics using Streptomyces thinghirensis (DSM 41919T) as a novel, bacteria-mediated synthesis pathway. METHODS: The ST@CuONPs were confirmed and characterized by UV-Vis spectroscopy, Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, particle-size analyzer, scanning electron microscopy (SEM), X-ray diffraction (XRD) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM). The antimicrobial and antibiofilm activities of ST@CuONPs were evaluated against Vancomycin-resistant Enterococcus faecium VRE ATCC 700221vanA, Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus NCTC 12493 and Ceftazidime-Resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa ATCC BAA-2108, as well as Vancomycin-sensitive Enterococcus faecalis ATCC 29212, Methicillin-sensitive Staphylococcus aureus ATCC 29213 and Ceftazidime-sensitive P. aeruginosa ATCC 27853. RESULTS AND DISCUSSION: TEM analysis revealed a spherical shape distribution of ST@CuONPs with an average size of ∼9.8 ± 0.27 nm. The ST@CuONPs demonstrated broad-spectrum antibacterial and antibiofilm activities to ward Multidrug-resistant bacteria. In addition, among the tested multi-drug resistant (MDR) pathogens, the highest antibacterial and antibiofilm efficacies were observed against the Gram-positive strain E. faecium VREATCC 700221vanA. The bacterial biofilm was reduced by 64% ± 0.58% at 1/4 × MIC, 83% ± 3% at 1/2 × MIC and 89% ± 1.15% at 1×MIC of ST@CuONP. CONCLUSION: The synthesis of ST@CuONPs using S. thinghirensis is an eco-friendly and economical method that avoids the use of toxic reagents. The resulting nanoparticles exhibit a potential to be explored as an alternative to conventional antibiotics.

articles.title: Comparative evaluation of the antibacterial activity and toxicity of a large panel of aminoglycoside antibiotics.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: There is a critical need for the development of novel antibiotics due to widespread occurrence of multidrug resistance. Despite their adverse effects, namely, nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity, the emergence of multi-drug resistant bacteria that are resistant to potent antibiotics such as the fluoroquinolones and the ß-lactams has highlighted the prominent role of aminoglycoside antibiotics (AGs). METHODS: We carried out a comprehensive comparative characterization of the antibacterial efficacy of a whole series of AGs and AG congeners against a large panel of 61 well characterized ESKAPE clinical isolates, and investigated their ototoxic and nephrotoxic potential, using the OC-k3 and HEI-OC1 otic cell lines and the kidney LLC-PK1 cell line, respectively, all under a common set of experimental conditions; additionally, a selection of these AGs was tested on murine cochlear explants; this information is not available in the literature. RESULTS: Out of 26 AGs tested, eight commercial AGs and four AG congeners demonstrated strong antibacterial activity against multi-drug resistant pathogens. Eight commercial AGs (amikacin, apramycin, gentamicin, isepamicin, neomycin, paromomycin, sisomicin and tobramycin) and four AG congeners (gentamicin C1a, C2, C2a and neomycin B) demonstrated strong antibacterial activity. Amikacin and isepamicin did not exert toxicity on murine cochlear explants. In addition, amikacin was the only one that did not exert significant nephrotoxicity on the LLC-PK1 cell line. Work on cochlear explants identified neomycin B and gentamicin C1a congeners as less ototoxic than their corresponding AG mixtures, although the congeners were more nephrotoxic. Importantly, we have for the first time directly compared the antibacterial activity and toxicity of seven of the most common gentamicin congeners. We identified gentamicin congeners B1 and X2 as highly toxic, while exhibiting very low antibacterial activity. CONCLUSION: We have demonstrated the utility of natural and semi-synthetic AGs against a large panel of multidrug-resistant clinical isolates present in our hospitals. We carried out a comparative assessment of the nephro- and ototoxicity of all these AGs and our data particularly highlighted a very high toxicity of the gentamicin congeners B1 and X2; these congeners may be present in small amounts in commercial gentamicin mixtures and their high toxicity, generally overlooked, could have serious negative implications when gentamicin formulations are applied in the clinic. Nonetheless, it must be taken into account that these studies were conducted on cell lines and, although the concentrations of AGs that are recorded in patients' plasma are variable, -depending on factors such as dosing regimens and the infectious agent-, the AG concentrations we applied to the cultures are well above these concentrations; confirmation of these results in in vivo models will thus be required.

articles.title: Pharmacokinetics of isoflurane uptake and disposition in piglets.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Isoflurane is a cardioprotective inhalational anesthetic widely used in cardiac surgery, but prior studies focused primarily on uptake parameters. We examined both uptake and disposition in piglets using inspiratory, end-tidal, arterial, and mixed venous concentrations. METHODS: Seven piglets received a fixed inspiratory concentration of 2% isoflurane during a 2-h uptake phase, followed by a 2-h disposition phase. Inspiratory and end-tidal concentrations were measured using an infrared analyzer. Femoral arterial blood and pulmonary artery mixed venous blood were sampled to determine isoflurane concentrations via gas chromatography at 1, 3, 5, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 80, 100, and 120 min during both uptake and disposition phases. Hemodynamic and respiratory parameters were recorded simultaneously. Body uptake and disposition rates were calculated by multiplying the difference between arterial and pulmonary artery blood concentrations by cardiac output. RESULTS: The rates of isoflurane body uptake increased gradually during the initial 20 min, reaching 20.7 mL min-1, before slowly declining to 10.5 mL min-1 by 120 min. Continuous decreases in washout rates were observed during the subsequent disposition phase. The concentration-time curves for end-tidal, arterial blood, and pulmonary artery blood concentrations fit well with zero-order input and first-order disposition kinetics. Arterial and pulmonary artery blood concentrations were best modeled by a two-compartment system. Only 14.5% of the isoflurane accumulated during the 2-h uptake phase was eliminated during the subsequent 2-h disposition phase. CONCLUSION: Under a fixed inspiratory isoflurane concentration, body uptake in piglets was empirically approximated by a zero-order input process over the modeled 120-min uptake interval, whereas the subsequent 2-h disposition phase followed first-order kinetics and was best described by a two-compartment pharmacokinetic model.

articles.title: Among rural older adults, an apparent physical-activity contrast in nonblank medication-field presence was markedly attenuated when chronic-disease management registration was incorporated into the analysis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Medication fields created for chronic-disease management may mislead when reused as medication-exposure measures in broader older-adult populations. Using routine exercise-frequency as routine-recorded physical activity (PA), we compared PA + records (daily, at least weekly, or occasional exercise) with PA- records (no exercise) and examined how nonblank medication-field presence changed after management-registration context was incorporated. METHODS: This cross-sectional study used 2,270 examination records from a 2025 rural primary-care program in northeastern China; PA was available for 2,226 records. The outcome was any nonblank text in the main-medication field. Modified Poisson regression estimated prevalence ratios (PRs) with small-sample-adjusted cluster-robust inference across 20 sites. Sequential models incorporated demographics, site, and four hypertension/diabetes management-registration categories. Logistic regression estimated standardized proportions and absolute differences. Medication text underwent secondary audit, including 200 randomly sampled retained entries independently reviewed by two pharmacists. RESULTS: Nonblank medication fields occurred in 1,114/1,157 (96.3%) records with hypertension and/or diabetes management registration versus 27/1,113 (2.4%) with neither registration. Field presence was low without registration and near-complete with hypertension-only or dual registration; the diabetes-only stratum was small (n = 37). Overall field presence was 56.4% in PA+ and 42.8% in PA- records (PR 1.317, 95% CI 1.076-1.612). After registration context was incorporated, the PR was 1.001 (95% CI 0.960-1.043); full adjustment yielded 1.002 (95% CI 0.959-1.046). Standardized proportions were 51.26% and 51.14%, a difference of 0.12 percentage points (95% CI -2.07 to 2.30). Among 1,368 retained entries, archived labels classified 75.9% as antihypertensive, 14.5% as glucose-lowering, 0.5% as other cardiovascular, 1.7% as other medications, and 7.4% as unresolved. Inter-reviewer agreement for broad therapeutic class was 99.5% (κ = 0.982), and parser-manual-reference concordance was 99.0%; these assessments did not verify medication exposure. CONCLUSION: Nonblank main-medication-field recording was strongly patterned by chronic-disease management registration, and the apparent overall PA-related contrast was markedly attenuated after this context was incorporated. Blank fields cannot establish medication nonuse, and nonblank or consistently parsed text cannot establish complete, current medication exposure.

articles.title: A comparative analysis of the effect of different drying treatments on the volatile organic compounds of polygonati odorati rhizoma.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Polygonati Odorati Rhizoma (POR) is a widely recognized functional food, volatile organic compounds (VOCs) as one of their main active metabolites. Drying is a crucial link in the front-end of the product production chain. There have been no comparison investigations on the effects of different drying methods on the VOCs of POR. METHODS: Gas chromatography-ion mobility spectrometry (GC-IMS) was utilized to detect and analyze the VOCs of POR samples treated with vacuum freeze-drying (VFD), vacuum drying (VD), sun drying (SD), hot-air drying (HAD), and microwave drying (MD). Analytical methods including Principal Component Analysis (PCA), Cluster Analysis (CA), and Partial Least-Squares Discriminant Analysis (PLS-DA) were used. RESULTS: A total of 56 VOCs were detected. Principal component analysis (PCA), cluster analysis (CA), and partial least-squares discriminant analysis (PLS-DA), consistently showed that the VOCs of VFD- and MD-treated samples were the closest to those of SD samples, whereas VD and HAD differed more markedly. Representative drying-specific markers tentatively identified as (E)-2-heptenal and ethyl hexanoate in SD, 2,5-dimethyl thiophene in HAD, (E)-2-butenal in MD, 2-butanol in VD, and 3-methyl-3-buten-1-ol in VFD were observed. CONCLUSIONS: These results indicate that different drying methods significantly affect the VOC profile of POR. VFD and MD are promising for VOC retention.

articles.title: Chrysin-loaded PCL nanocapsule spray as a topical strategy against cutaneous candidiasis.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Candida albicans, the most prevalent fungal pathogen in humans, poses increasing therapeutic challenges due to rising resistance to conventional azole antifungals, driving interest in natural alternatives. Chrysin (5,7- dihydroxyflavone) is a flavonoid with promising biological activities that are limited by poor aqueous solubility and low bioavailability. This study aimed to develop and characterize chrysin-loaded poly (ε-caprolactone) (PCL) nanocapsules in a spray formulation for topical treatment of cutaneous candidiasis. METHODS: Nanocapsules were produced by interfacial deposition of the preformed polymer and characterized for particle size, zeta potential, encapsulation efficiency, and morphology. Their performance was further evaluated through in vitro release studies, antifungal activity against C. albicans, antioxidant activity, and spray performance. RESULTS AND DISCUSSION: The formulation exhibited nanometric size (207.6 ± 4.63 nm), low polydispersity (0.174 ± 0.04), high encapsulation efficiency (87.28% ± 0.77%), and sustained drug release over 120 h, with antifungal activity substantially superior to free chrysin, requiring 5- to 8-fold lower concentrations to achieve equivalent inhibitory and fungicidal effects, and enhanced antioxidant efficacy at lower concentrations. The spray device delivered consistent and reproducible doses (118.5% of theoretical content, RSD 5.78%). These findings demonstrate that chrysin-loaded PCL nanocapsules successfully overcome solubility limitations, enhance antifungal and antioxidant activities, and provide sustained release, representing a promising nanotechnology-based alternative for cutaneous candidiasis treatment with convenient topical application.

articles.title: Exploring the impact of GLP-1 analogues and DPP-4 inhibitors on cognitive decline in elderly patients with type 2 diabetes: a competing risks analysis from a real-world cohort.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Older adults with type 2 diabetes (T2DM) face an increased risk of cognitive decline. While glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) have shown neuroprotective effects, comparative evidence versus dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors (DPP-4i) in real-world older populations is limited. METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study using health administrative data, including individuals aged ≥65 initiating GLP-1RAs or DPP-4i therapy between 2010 and 2018. Patients with prior cognitive disorders were excluded. The primary outcome was a composite of incident cognitive disorders or death. Analyses were adjusted for clinical and demographic characteristics. Marginal structural models and competing risks methods were used to estimate treatment effects. Both an 'As treated' (AT) and an 'Intention to Treat' (ITT) designs were employed. RESULTS: A total of 2,579 individuals were included (GLP-1RAs: 393; DPP-4i: 2,186), with a median follow-up of 44 months in the AT analysis. GLP-1RAs users had a lower risk of the composite outcome, especially in the early follow-up (HR at 2 years: 0.5 [95% CI: 0.26-0.93]). Competing-risk analysis showed a lower early risk of death without prior cognitive disorders among GLP-1RA initiators. The point estimate of sub-distribution HR was 0.4 also for cognitive disorders, yet not statistically significant because of the small number of events. CONCLUSION: GLP-1RAs use was associated with a lower early risk of the composite outcome of cognitive disorders or death compared with DPP-4i in older adults with T2DM. The observed association with cognitive disorders alone was directionally consistent with a potentially lower risk, but the very small number of events precludes firm conclusions regarding a protective effect on cognitive outcomes. Longer follow-up and cognitive-specific evaluations are needed to confirm these associations.

articles.title: Real-world comparative outcomes of pyrotinib-based versus pertuzumab-based first-line therapy in HER2-Positive advanced breast cancer: a multicenter retrospective cohort study from Xinjiang, China.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Direct comparative evidence between taxane plus trastuzumab plus pyrotinib (THPyro) and taxane plus trastuzumab plus pertuzumab (THP) as first-line therapy for HER2-positive advanced breast cancer remains limited. METHODS: This multicenter retrospective real-world cohort study included 181 female patients in Xinjiang, China who initiated first-line THP or THPyro between 1 January 2020 and 30 September 2025. Propensity score matching generated 60 matched pairs. The primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS). Median follow-up in the matched cohort was 28.4 months. RESULTS: After matching, baseline characteristics were well balanced. THPyro showed numerically longer median PFS than THP (20.1 vs. 17.6 months; log-rank P = 0.086), and the stratified Cox model showed a non-significant trend toward reduced progression risk (hazard ratio, 0.478; 95% confidence interval, 0.216-1.061). Restricted mean survival time (RMST) analysis demonstrated a significant 24-month PFS gain with THPyro (absolute difference, 2.41 months; P = 0.007). Objective response and disease control rates were comparable. Brain metastasis status was the most prominent potential effect modifier, with an exploratory signal observed in patients with baseline brain metastases. THPyro was associated with more diarrhea, and higher albumin level and prophylactic loperamide use were associated with a lower observed risk of grade ≥2 diarrhea. CONCLUSION: First-line THPyro was associated with a non-significant trend toward longer PFS and a significant 24-month RMST gain compared with THP in this retrospective matched cohort. An exploratory signal was observed among patients with baseline brain metastases, while diarrhea was more frequent and required proactive management.

articles.title: Ellagic acid promoted efficacy of oxaliplatin on wild-type TP53 colorectal cancer via regulating ataxia-telangiectasia mutated protein kinase and Wip1.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Drug resistance in colorectal cancer frequently leads to chemotherapy failure. The application of small-molecule compounds to enhance chemotherapy efficacy has become a common therapeutic strategy. Ellagic acid, a natural polyphenol in plants, is abundantly contained in herbal medicines used for adjuvant chemotherapy against colorectal cancer. Nevertheless, the regulatory effect of ellagic acid on oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy remains unclear. METHODS: Cell Counting Kit-8 and colony formation assays were used to evaluate the efffcacy of the combination of ellagic acid and oxaliplatin. Network pharmacology, Human Phospho-Kinase Array, co-immunoprecipitation and thermal shift assay were used to screen potential targets of ellagic acid in chemotherapy sensitization. Transfection of overexpression plasmids and shRNAs against these targets was performed to verify the underlying mechanism. Tumor tissues derived from colorectal cancer patients were used to establish PDX models for in vivo experiments. All cells and tissues used in this study have wild-type TP53. RESULTS: Cellular experiments demonstrated that ellagic acid exerts a synergistic effect with oxaliplatin. Target screening revealed that ellagic acid inhibits Wip1, thereby upregulating p53 and resulting in the synergistic anti-tumor effect. Further studies demonstrated that ellagic acid interacts to ATM and suppresses ATM phosphorylation, thereby downregulating Wip1 via the ATM/ AMPK/HIPK2 signaling pathway. Data from FOLFOX chemotherapy indicated that high Wip1 expression correlates with poor prognosis. PDX models demonstrated that ellagic acid enhances the therapeutic efficacy of oxaliplatin, particularly in tumors with high Wip1 expression. DISCUSSION: Our findings indicate that ellagic acid enhances the antitumor efficacy of oxaliplatin in colorectal cancer with wild-type TP53 and high Wip1 expression.

articles.title: Engineered probiotic-mediated palmitoylethanolamide biosynthesis protects against colitis-associated liver injury.
articles.abstract: Chronic colitis promotes secondary liver injury through disruption of the gut-liver axis, whereby intestinal barrier breakdown enables portal translocation of microbial products that activate hepatic inflammatory and fibrogenic pathways. Palmitoylethanolamide (PEA), an endogenous ALIAmide acting primarily via PPAR-α, exerts anti-inflammatory and barrier-protective effects, but its clinical use is limited by poor oral bioavailability. We investigated whether mucosa-targeted, probiotic-mediated, in situ PEA biosynthesis could attenuate liver injury associated with chronic colitis. Male C57BL/6J mice were subjected to chronic dextran sulfate sodium (DSS) colitis and treated with an engineered Lactobacillus paracasei F19 strain expressing human NAPE-PLD (pNAPE-LP) plus ultra-low-dose palmitate, a control strain (pLP), or pNAPE-LP combined with the PPAR-α antagonist MK886. pNAPE-LP significantly increased colonic PEA levels and elevated circulating and hepatic PEA, confirming effective local production with systemic distribution. Treatment ameliorated colitis severity, restored tight-junction protein expression, and reduced endotoxemia. Importantly, pNAPE-LP attenuated colitis-associated liver injury by decreasing histological damage and collagen deposition, lowering transaminase levels, and reducing hepatic neutrophil infiltration. These effects were accompanied by the suppression of the hepatic TLR4/NF-κB/NLRP3 inflammasome axis, reduced caspase-1 activation, decreased IL-1β, TNF-α, and IL-6 levels, restored PPAR-α expression, and reduced Bax expression. The control strain was ineffective, and PPAR-α inhibition abolished both intestinal and hepatic protection. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that engineered probiotics acting as "living drug factories" can target the gut-liver axis via localized PEA biosynthesis, restoring barrier integrity and limiting hepatic inflammatory and fibrogenic signaling in chronic colitis.

articles.title: Integrative network toxicology and pharmacology reveal that kaempferol alleviates BaP-triggered pulmonary fibrosis via suppressing Ras/COX-2-dependent cellular senescence.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a chronic, progressive lung disease. Benzo[a]pyrene (BaP), a major constituent of cigarette smoke and air pollution, has been closely associated with pulmonary fibrosis. However, its molecular mechanism remains unclear. The natural flavonoid kaempferol possesses anti-inflammatory and antioxidant properties. However, its effects and mechanisms in BaP-induced pulmonary fibrosis remain unclear. OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to predict potential targets of BaP-induced fibrosis and kaempferol intervention in BaP-induced IPF, and to validate whether kaempferol reverses BaP-induced epithelial senescence and fibrosis via the Ras/COX-2 signaling pathway in vitro. METHODS: Network toxicology, network pharmacology, machine learning, and molecular docking were integrated to predict potential targets of BaP-induced fibrosis and kaempferol intervention, followed by GO and KEGG pathway enrichment analyses. Additionally, virtual knockout analysis was performed to explore the regulatory relationships among Ras, COX-2, and cellular senescence. MLE-12 cells were used as an in vitro model, and senescence-related indicators were assessed by SA-β-gal staining, Western blot, and ELISA. RESULTS: KEGG enrichment analysis revealed that these targets were significantly enriched in the Ras signaling pathway. Molecular docking confirmed that kaempferol exhibited good binding affinity for the above target proteins. Cell experiments demonstrated that BaP significantly promoted cellular senescence and activated Ras and COX-2. Kaempferol treatment effectively reversed these changes. CONCLUSION: This study reveals that BaP promotes IPF by inducing epithelial cell senescence via the Ras/COX-2 signaling pathway. Kaempferol may exert anti-fibrotic effects by counteracting this pathway-mediated senescence. These findings provide a theoretical basis for the pulmonary fibrosis effects of BaP and support kaempferol as a potential anti-fibrotic agent.

articles.title: A real-world pharmacovigilance study of FDA adverse event reporting system events for bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide.
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Bictegravir/emtricitabine/tenofovir alafenamide (B/F/TAF) is a widely used antiretroviral regimen, but its real-world long-term safety profile in diverse populations remains incompletely characterized. METHODS: We analyzed adverse drug signals from the FAERS database (2018-2025) with B/F/TAF as the primary suspected drug. Disproportionality analyses using reporting odds ratio (ROR), proportional reporting ratio (PRR), Bayesian confidence propagation neural network (BCPNN), and multi-item gamma Poisson shrinker (MGPS) algorithms were performed to detect safety signals. RESULTS: A total of 6,816 case reports and 13,853 adverse events were included. The highest numbers of reports were related to "Injury, poisoning and procedural complications" (n = 1,792), followed by "General disorders and administration site conditions" (n = 1,726) and "Investigations" (n = 1,499). The System Organ Classes (SOCs) meeting all four disproportionality criteria were "Congenital, familial and genetic disorders" and "Pregnancy, puerperium and perinatal conditions." The most frequently reported preferred terms were weight increase (408 cases), product dose omission (242 cases), and maternal exposure during pregnancy (202 cases), while the strongest signals by ROR were viral load increased (ROR 160.14), CD4 lymphocytes decreased (ROR 124.60), and immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (ROR 88.12). Overall, 37.94% of events occurred within the first month of treatment, and 17.49% occurred after one year. CONCLUSION: These pharmacovigilance signals merit clinical awareness, particularly regarding metabolic monitoring, virologic/immunologic parameters (which likely reflect treatment response rather than drug toxicity), and pregnancy exposure reporting. Events occurred both early and late, reinforcing the necessity of longitudinal pharmacovigilance for this widely used antiretroviral regimen. However, these findings are exploratory and should not be interpreted as confirmed causal associations.

articles.title: Treprostinil Inhalation Powder for Pulmonary Arterial Hypertension: Evidence and Clinical Positioning Among Inhaled Formulations.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To describe treprostinil inhalation powder (Yutrepia) and evaluate its role among inhaled treprostinil formulations for pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). DATA SOURCES: PubMed/MEDLINE was searched from inception through September 10, 2026 using terms related to PAH, treprostinil, inhaled treprostinil, dry powder inhalers, Tyvaso, Tyvaso dry powder inhalation (DPI), Yutrepia, and LIQ861. The search identified 258 records; reference lists and prescribing information were also reviewed. STUDY SELECTION AND DATA EXTRACTION: Twelve original reports addressing efficacy, safety, pharmacokinetics, transition, or administration were included. One author performed initial screening and study selection, and a second author independently verified inclusion and exclusion decisions. DATA SYNTHESIS: TRIUMPH I demonstrated a placebo-corrected median improvement of 20 m in peak 6MWD at week 12 with nebulized treprostinil added to oral PAH therapy. BREEZE supported transition feasibility, comparable exposure, and greater device satisfaction after transition to treprostinil DPI; INSPIRE supported Yutrepia tolerability and acceptability, but its exploratory efficacy outcomes were descriptive. No head-to-head trial has established superiority.Relevance to Patient Care and Clinical Practice in Comparison With Existing Drugs:Both dry powder formulations reduce nebulizer equipment burden, but current evidence does not establish greater efficacy, safety, adherence, or convenience for one dry powder product over the other. Selection should consider disease risk, device technique, tolerability, treatment burden, cost, coverage, and access. CONCLUSIONS: Yutrepia expands inhaled prostacyclin options for PAH. Selection should be individualized, and inhaled therapy should not be considered equivalent to parenteral prostacyclin when parenteral treatment is clinically indicated.

articles.title: Use of firsekibart for acute gouty arthritis in a maintenance hemodialysis patient with multiple high-risk comorbidities: a case report.
articles.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To describe the clinical course of Firsekibart treatment for acute gouty arthritis in a 51-year-old patient receiving maintenance hemodialysis with multiple high-risk comorbidities, focusing on the temporal relationship among dialysis, drug administration and the timing of symptom changes. This report adds to the limited evidence on using Firsekibart, a novel fully human monoclonal antibody targeting IL-1β, in patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis. METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed the patient's underlying diseases, acute gout manifestations, timing of Firsekibart administration relative to hemodialysis, visual analogue scale (VAS) pain scores, body temperature, and inflammatory markers. The clinical course was interpreted in the context of available clinical evidence on Firsekibart, experience with other IL-1 pathway agents in patients with advanced chronic kidney disease and/or receiving dialysis, and monoclonal antibody pharmacokinetics. RESULTS: Pain relief was documented 6-7 h after Firsekibart administration, before the first post-dose hemodialysis session; however, tramadol and topical flurbiprofen had been administered within the preceding hour and may have contributed to the observed improvement. No worsening or rebound of pain was observed on the day of dialysis or the following day. No immediate hypersensitivity reaction was observed during the early post-dose period. Follow-up continued through 24 June 2026 (35 days post-dose), no gout flare recurred; however, biliary symptoms and a febrile episode with suspected catheter-related bloodstream infection occurred, with uncertain relationships to Firsekibart. CONCLUSION: In this maintenance hemodialysis patient, gout-related pain improved before the first post-dose dialysis session and did not rebound after dialysis. However, this single case, without pre- or post-dialysis Firsekibart concentration measurements, cannot establish causality or determine the effect of hemodialysis on drug exposure.

articles.title: Case Report: Four-year durable remission, cerebral oligoprogression, and femoral head necrosis following severe recurrent immune checkpoint inhibitor-related pneumonitis in a patient with stage IV lung adenocarcinoma.
articles.abstract: Severe immune checkpoint inhibitor-related pneumonitis (CIP) typically leads to the permanent discontinuation of immunotherapy; however, its long-term oncological outcomes and late drug toxicity remain poorly defined. This report describes a patient with stage IV lung adenocarcinoma who, following recurrent grade 3 CIP, achieved durable systemic remission for more than 4 years and displayed a distinctive pattern of cerebral oligoprogression. A 66-year-old male patient with stage IV lung adenocarcinoma achieved a partial response (PR) after four cycles of sintilimab combined with chemotherapy. Three weeks after the last dose, he developed grade 3 CIP complicated by acute pulmonary embolism. Recurrence occurred twice because of overly rapid corticosteroid tapering and was ultimately controlled through an ultralow tapering regimen (50 mg/day prednisone initially, reduced by 5 mg per week) combined with pirfenidone for antifibrotic therapy. Following the resolution of CIP, no further systemic antitumor therapy was administered. During 48 months of follow-up, the patient maintained complete remission (CR) of extracranial metastases; the sole site of progression was a solitary cerebellar lesion, which exhibited three episodes of oligoprogression, each of which was successfully managed with either radiotherapy or bevacizumab-based therapy. At 34 months after the onset of CIP, the patient developed bilateral osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH), with right-sided slight collapse (ARCO stage III) and left-sided stage I. This case suggests a potential synergistic toxic mechanism between cumulative corticosteroid exposure (approximately 7,300 mg prednisone equivalents) and VEGF inhibition-mediated microvascular injury. This case also suggests that ultralow corticosteroid tapering combined with antifibrotic therapy can effectively manage refractory CIP; the dissociation between durable peripheral immunological memory and isolated central nervous system (CNS) progression supports the hypothesis of CNS immune privilege. Finally, clinicians must remain vigilant about long-term musculoskeletal toxicity in long-term survivors of ICI therapy.

articles.title: Factors Affecting Tacrolimus Levels in Pediatric Liver Transplant Recipients During the Early Posttransplant Period.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Tacrolimus is the cornerstone of immunosuppression in pediatric liver transplantation (LT) but exhibits high pharmacokinetic variability. OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to identify clinical and laboratory determinants of tacrolimus trough levels (C0) during the initial 14 days posttransplant. METHODS: This retrospective study analyzed pediatric LT recipients (January 2020-October 2025). We evaluated continuous variables for normality using the Shapiro-Wilk test and analyzed them with nonparametric bivariate tests, including Spearman's rank correlation and Mann-Whitney U tests. To account for repeated measurements within individual patients, we fitted a linear mixed-effects model with a random intercept. Backward elimination with a conservative threshold of p > 0.50 was applied to remove nonsignificant variables, while retaining predefined clinical covariates. Model fit was evaluated using Akaike Information Criterion (AIC) and Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC), and the final parsimonious model was selected by minimizing BIC while excluding individual antimicrobial treatments to prevent overfitting. To quantify complex polypharmacy and avoid overfitting, we created a Pharmacological Interaction Score (PIS) by assigning weighted positive or negative values to co-administered medications based on their known CYP3A4/5 inhibitory or inducing effects on tacrolimus. RESULTS: In 33 patients, hemoglobin (β = 0.78, P < .001) and serum creatinine (β = 3.41, P < .001) were positively associated with tacrolimus levels, while INR showed a negative association (β = -1.00, P = .036). The model included albumin, a pharmacologic interaction score designed to simplify complex polypharmacy into a single numerical value, as well as platelet counts, which were retained but not statistically significant. Tacrolimus levels were not significantly influenced by sepsis, nutrition (enteral/parenteral), or extracorporeal therapies. CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: In this cohort, clinical complications such as sepsis, nutritional support methods, and extracorporeal therapies did not significantly affect drug trough levels. These results suggest that early postoperative fluctuations in whole-blood tacrolimus levels are mainly driven by patient hematological status, renal function, and graft recovery. Clinically, including hematological and biochemical parameters in routine drug monitoring could improve dose management and help prevent unnecessary empirical changes during critical care.

articles.title: A Pilot Study to Describe Symptomatic Hyperammonemia Secondary to Recombinant Erwinia Asparaginase.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: Asparaginase therapy is essential for the treatment of pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma (ALL/LLy). For patients who develop hypersensitivity to a first-line Escherichia coli (E. coli)-derived product, the standard of care is to transition to an Erwinia-derived product. Given that all asparaginase products exert their antileukemic effects by enzymatically breaking down asparagine to aspartic acid and ammonia, elevations in ammonia levels are anticipated during asparaginase treatment. However, symptomatic hyperammonemia is not expected. Recombinant Erwinia asparaginase is relatively new to the market, and there have been several case reports of symptomatic hyperammonemia with this specific formulation. OBJECTIVES: The primary objective of this prospective study was to establish the incidence of symptomatic hyperammonemia secondary to recombinant Erwinia asparaginase and to determine if a larger, multicenter trial was warranted. Additional objectives included identifying potential risk factors for symptomatic hyperammonemia. METHODS: This single-center, prospective trial received institutional review board approval. Funding was provided by the Mayo Clinic Clinical and Translational Science Award (grant number: UL1TR002377) and the Mayo Clinic Department of Pharmacy. All patients treated by the pediatric hematology/oncology team at our institution who were receiving recombinant Erwinia asparaginase were eligible. Patients were excluded if they were less than 1 year of age at study entry. Enrolled participants had a baseline plasma ammonia level obtained, followed by twice weekly ammonia levels while receiving recombinant Erwinia asparaginase. Aside from baseline, all ammonia levels were trough levels measured either 48 h or 72 h after the previous dose. RESULTS: Five patients were included, three of whom were male (60%). Three patients had T-cell ALL (60%), one patient had B-cell ALL (20%), and one patient had infantile B-cell ALL (20%). The median age was 5 years (range 1-14). Two patients were followed for two courses of recombinant Erwinia asparaginase, and the remaining patients were followed for a single course. Median baseline plasma ammonia level was 12 μmol/L. Median ammonia level while receiving recombinant Erwinia asparaginase was 146 μmol/L. Three patients (60%) developed symptomatic hyperammonemia with a median ammonia level of 174 μmol/L (range 108-343). The reported symptoms were nausea (100%), fatigue (66.7%), and decreased appetite (33.3%). The remaining two patients experienced asymptomatic hyperammonemia with a median ammonia level of 125 μmol/L (range 55-304). CONCLUSIONS: Based on our small cohort, symptomatic hyperammonemia may be a common adverse effect for patients receiving recombinant Erwinia asparaginase. Evaluating plasma ammonia levels appears reasonable in patients who are experiencing nausea or other symptoms of hyperammonemia. Additional studies are warranted to further characterize this toxicity.
